<system-reminder>
## Swarm Mode

You are now in "agent swarm" mode. The user may send tasks that require a large number of parallel subagents.

## Workflow

You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

2. After exploring, if you are convinced no subagent is needed to complete the task, tell the user why and wait for further instructions; otherwise, continue with the appropriate delegation.

3. Once you have enough context, do not handle the main work yourself. Use AgentSwarm with a `prompt_template` containing the `{{item}}` placeholder and an `items` array for the requested or appropriate number of subagents, partitioning the problem so each item gives one subagent a distinct part of the work. Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.
- Unless the user explicitly specifies a lower limit, do not try to conserve the number of agents. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. If the subagents only need to read, inspect, or report back without making changes, their scopes may overlap slightly.
</system-reminder>

=== yarn-unguava-preconditions ===
title: 'HADOOP-18017. unguava: remove Preconditions from hadoop-yarn-project modules'
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  The YARN codebase is still carrying Guava Preconditions calls in multiple modules even though the project is moving away from that dependency. Maintainers need those usages removed without changing the observable behavior of the affected APIs.


  ## Desired outcome

  Replace the remaining Guava Preconditions usages in the targeted hadoop-yarn-project modules with Hadoop or JDK equivalents while preserving current exception types, messages, and control flow. This is an internal refactor only.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The YARN modules build without the removed Guava Preconditions references, and the touched code paths continue to reject invalid inputs the same way they did before.

  '
=== dfsadmin-system-err ===
title: HDFS-16525.System.err should be used when error occurs in multiple methods in DFSAdmin class
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Administrators using `hdfs dfsadmin` need successful command output and failure output to be separated cleanly so scripts, consoles, and support workflows can tell the difference between normal results and errors. Today several DFSAdmin paths print error messages to standard output, which makes failures harder to detect and can pollute machine-readable command output.


  ## Desired outcome

  DFSAdmin should send operational failures to `System.err` while preserving the existing success messages and command semantics. Commands that succeed should continue to report through normal output, but when a command fails the user should see the failure on stderr instead of mixed into stdout.


  ## Acceptance signals

  DFSAdmin success cases keep their current visible output, failure cases are emitted on `System.err`, mixed HA command scenarios preserve the existing messages, and users or scripts can distinguish command errors from normal stdout reliably.

  '
=== ipc-multi-connection-throughput ===
title: HADOOP-13144. Enhancing IPC client throughput via multiple connections per user
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Hadoop service running very high IPC call volumes to the same endpoint can bottleneck on a single client-side connection per user, even when the workload itself is highly parallel.


  ## Desired outcome

  Operators and framework code should be able to open more than one logical client connection for the same address, protocol, and user when they deliberately vary the connection identity, instead of being forced through one shared channel. The public RPC surface needs to make that possible by accepting a caller-supplied `Client.ConnectionId` in `RPC.getProtocolProxy(...)`, so advanced clients can spread traffic without forking the whole RPC stack.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Using `RPC.getProtocolProxy` with distinct `Client.ConnectionId` instances should yield independent client proxies and allow the same principal to drive parallel request streams to one server. Existing call semantics, security initialization, and retry behavior from the `ConnectionId` must remain intact.

  '
=== dfsadmin-reconfig-livenodes ===
title: HDFS-16568. dfsadmin -reconfig option to start/query reconfig on all live datanodes
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators often need to start, inspect, or list reconfiguration work across every live DataNode instead of targeting one IPC address at a time.

  ## Desired outcome

  `dfsadmin -reconfig` should accept `livenodes` for DataNode bulk operations, so `-reconfig datanode livenodes start|status|properties` can fan out across the live cluster while preserving the existing single-host form for NameNodes and individual DataNodes.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Bulk DataNode requests report per-node outcomes, unsupported bulk use for non-DataNode targets is rejected clearly, and the command finishes with a cluster-level success summary.

  '

title: HDFS-16327. Make dfs.namenode.max.slowpeer.collect.nodes reconfigurable
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  NameNode operators may need to adjust how many slow peers are retained for reporting without scheduling a restart. Today dfs.namenode.max.slowpeer.collect.nodes behaves like a static setting, which makes live tuning awkward.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make dfs.namenode.max.slowpeer.collect.nodes live-reconfigurable on the NameNode and expose it through the standard reconfigurable-properties listing. Valid changes should take effect immediately in DatanodeManager.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Administrators can reconfigure dfs.namenode.max.slowpeer.collect.nodes at runtime, observe the updated value through the running NameNode, and see the property listed among the NameNode''s reconfigurable settings.

  '

title: HDFS-16540 Data locality is lost when DataNode pod restarts in kubern…
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  In Kubernetes-style deployments, a DataNode pod can restart with the same DataNode identity but a different IP address. If the NameNode keeps the old host-to-DataNode mapping around, clients and colocated services can lose data locality because the stale IP is still treated as the preferred host.


  ## Desired outcome

  When a DataNode re-registers with the same UUID but a new IP address, the NameNode should replace the old host mapping with the new one so locality decisions follow the live pod location. This should preserve the existing registration semantics while ensuring stale IP entries do not continue to influence host lookups or block-location ordering.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Re-registration with the same DataNode identity removes the obsolete host entry, the new IP becomes the active host mapping for that DataNode, locality-sensitive block locations prefer the current IP rather than the stale one, and restarting a DataNode pod no longer causes persistent locality loss.

  '

<!--
Thanks for sending a pull request!
  1. If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/HADOOP/How+To+Contribute
  2. Make sure your PR title starts with JIRA issue id, e.g., 'HADOOP-17799. Your PR title ...'.
-->

### Description of PR
The source files for `hdfs_count`, `hdfs_mkdir` and `hdfs_rm` uses `getopt` for parsing the command line arguments. getopt is available only on Linux and thus, isn't cross platform. We need to replace getopt with `boost::program_options` to make these tools cross platform.

### How was this patch tested?
This PR was tested by running the above tools locally.

## hdfs_mkdir

Ran the tool to create a directory.

```bash
$ ./hdfs_mkdir /home/gautham/new-dir
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10280768/151838650-55a1fc41-8d4c-4d72-9a3b-563cfd37857d.png)

The tool is then run with\
  \ the `-p` option to exercise the creation of intermediate directories.

```bash
$ ./hdfs_mkdir -p /home/gautham/a/b/c
```

The trailing `a/b/c` directories are created under the path `/home/gautham`.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10280768/151836730-3f228afc-720f-4518-be93-0e656cb6969a.png)

The tool is then run with the `-m` option with `700` as the mode. This turns all the permission bits on for user and turns off all the permission bits for group and other users.

```bash
$ ./hdfs_mkdir -p -m 700 /home/gautham/d/e/f
```

The trailing `d/e/f` directories are created under the path `/home/gautham` with the permission of `700`, even for the intermediate directories.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10280768/151837549-a435e367-c513-45ed-8e38-4591e020fe68.png)

Confirmation from browser.

![Browser](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10280768/151837719-dcf51ce5-6b94-4796-9abb-347b2a727460.jpg)

<hr>

## hdfs_count
\
  
Ran the tool on one of the HDFS paths.

```bash
$ ./hdfs_co
"

payload.output:
title: HADOOP-17995. Stale record should be remove when DataNodePeerMetrics#dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  DataNode peer metrics are used for diagnosing downstream packet latency, but stale peers should not remain in the JSON dump after their rolling window has expired.


  ## Desired outcome

  `dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson` should drop stale records instead of continuing to report them.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The JSON output contains only peers with current rolling-average data rather than expired entries that confuse troubleshooting.

  '
=====
title: HADOOP-17995. Stale record should be remove when DataNodePeerMetrics#dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using DataNodePeerMetrics need dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson() to reflect only currently valid peer timing data. Stale entries should disappear once their rolling-average windows expire, otherwise the JSON keeps advertising dead peers as active.


  ## Desired outcome

  Restore stale-record removal for the peer downstream timing JSON while keeping active peers visible until their data truly expires. This should apply to the JSON dump itself, not just to internal statistics.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Before expiry, dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson() still lists the expected peer addresses; after the rolling window expires, those peers are removed and the JSON can collapse to {} when nothing current remains.

  '

args.prompt_template:
You are one of ~37 parallel agents implementing change requests in an Apache Hadoop repository at /workspace (checked out at an earlier state of the real project). Your assigned batch of requirement slugs is:

{{item}}

The slugs are listed after the batch name (which ends with a colon). For EACH slug, in the listed order:

1. Read /workspace/requirements/<slug>.yaml in full. It describes a real Apache JIRA change (the title contains the JIRA id, e.g. HDFS-16302). Implement that change in the codebase, faithfully reproducing the upstream Apache commit where you know or can infer it. Search the codebase to find the exact files involved. Keep changes minimal and consistent with surrounding code style.

2. Commit the requirement separately using this EXACT protocol (other agents work in the same repo concurrently, so the flock and the targeted pathspecs are mandatory):

flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c '
cd /workspace
git add -A -- <only the files you changed for this requirement>
git diff --cached > requirement_patches/<slug>.diff
test -s requirement_patches/<slug>.diff
git add -f requirement_patches/<slug>.diff
git commit -m "impl: <slug>"
'

Rules:
- NEVER run plain `git add -A` or `git add .` without a pathspec, and NEVER commit changes in files you did not edit for this requirement. `git status` may show other modified/untracked files — those belong to other agents; ignore them completely, do not revert or stage them.
- The .diff file MUST be non-empty (that is what `test -s` enforces). requirement_patches/*.diff matches `*.diff` in .gitignore, so `git add -f` is required for it.
- If your batch contains a slug starting with `revert-`, first implement and commit the corresponding non-revert slug (it reverts the change of the other slug in your batch), THEN implement the revert as its own commit.
- If two slugs in your batch describe the same upstream change (duplicate JIRA), implement the change for the first one; for the second, add the remaining parts of the upstream change (extra test coverage, remaining call sites, related cleanups) so its diff is also non-empty.
- Slugs with `-docs` or doc-style titles usually touch only markdown/site files; still commit them the same way.
- Do not modify anything under /workspace/requirements/ or other agents' requirement_patches files.
- Do not attempt a full Maven build (too slow, no network guarantees). A quick targeted `mvn -o -pl <module> compile -DskipTests` is optional; prefer careful code reading. You may add tests under /workspace/agent_tests/ if useful, but it is optional.
- If a requirement turns out to be already implemented in the tree, inspect `git log --oneline | head -50` and existing requirement_patches to confirm, then find the smallest genuine remaining delta of the upstream change and commit that; only skip the slug if absolutely no delta exists, and explain in your final report.

Work through ALL slugs in your batch; do not stop early. At the end, report a compact per-slug status list (slug: committed/skipped + one-line note).

2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context

12

3	requirement: '## Context

3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Engineers building MapReduce NativeTask on newer Fedora environments can hit a compiler failure as newer GCC toolchains enable C++17 rules that reject older exception-specification syntax. That turns a normal native build into a hard stop on otherwise supported developer machines.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The NativeTask build should compile cleanly on Fedora 34 and similar GCC 11+ environments without changing NativeTask behavior. This is a build-compatibility fix only, so the native package that gets produced should behave exactly as before once compilation succeeds.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  NativeTask no longer fails with the C++17 dynamic-exception-specification compiler error on Fedora 34+ toolchains, the native Maven build completes successfully, and no runtime behavior changes beyond restoring build compatibility.
16	
17	  '

17	  '

2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context

10	
11	  ## Acceptance signals
12	
13	  Data compressed through repeated `finish()` and `resetState()` cycles decompresses back to the complete original content instead of stopping after the first frame.
14	
15	  '

17	  '

15	  '
```

```
title: HADOOP-17932. Distcp file length comparison have no effect
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  DistCp jobs that resume a copy or write starting at a nonzero offset can transfer bytes successfully but still skip a meaningful final size check.


  ## Desired outcome

  After a non-split copy completes, DistCp should validate the destination against the amount actually written for that attempt, including the starting offset, so partial or append-style copies cannot be reported as successful when the final length is wrong.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The post-copy verification uses the effective copied length of `offset + bytesRead` rather than comparing the destination only with the original source length.

  '

title: HADOOP-15789. DistCp does not clean staging folder if class extends DistCp. Contributed by Lawrence Andrews.
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  Developers extending DistCp may subclass the main implementation and still expect the standard staging-directory cleanup to remain available instead of having to duplicate private shutdown logic.


  ## Desired outcome

  A DistCp subclass should be able to invoke `cleanup()` and get the same staging-folder removal behavior as the base implementation, including clearing the remembered staging location after cleanup runs.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Subclassed DistCp implementations can trigger `cleanup()` successfully, the staging metadata directory is removed, and the in-memory staging reference does not keep pointing at the old location afterward.

title: HADOOP-18125. Utility to identify git commit / Jira fixVersion discrepancies for RC preparation
category: bugfix
requirement: 'HADOOP-18125. Utility to identify git commit / Jira fixVersion discrepancies for RC preparation


  ### Description of PR

  As part of RC preparation,  we need to identify all git commits that landed on release branch, however their corresponding Jira is either not resolved yet or does not contain expected fixVersions. Only when we have git commits and corresponding Jiras with expected fixVersion resolved, we get all such Jiras included in auto-generated CHANGES.md as per Yetus changelog generator.


  Proposal of this Jira is to provide such script that can be useful for all upcoming RC preparations and list down all Jiras where we need manual intervention. This utility script should use Jira API to retrieve individual fields and use git log to loop through commit history.


  The script should identify these issues:


  1. commit is reverted as per commit message

  2. commit does not contain Jira number format (e.g. HADOOP-XXXX / HDFS-XXXX etc) in message

  3. Jira does not have expected fixVersion

  4. Jira has expected fixVersion, but it is not yet resolved

  5. Jira has release corresponding fixVersion and is resolved, but no corresponding commit yet found


  It can take inputs as:


  1. First commit hash to start excluding commits from history

  2. Fix Version

  3. JIRA Project Name

  4. Path of project''s working dir

  5. Jira server url


  ### How was this patch tested?

  Locally.

title: 'HDFS-16352. return the real datanode numBlocks in #getDatanodeStorage…'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  NameNode clients that inspect getDatanodeStorageReport expect the numBlocks field to reflect the DataNode''s actual block count. Returning a default zero there makes the report misleading for capacity planning and troubleshooting.


  ## Desired outcome

  Populate the DatanodeInfo inside getDatanodeStorageReport with the real live numBlocks value rather than relying on a builder copy path that loses that field. This should make the report consistent with the DataNode''s actual block inventory.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A storage report for a node that has blocks now returns a DatanodeInfo whose getNumBlocks value matches the real count instead of always falling back to zero.

  '
title: HDFS-16315. Add metrics related to Transfer and NativeCopy for DataNode
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  DataNode operators troubleshooting slow block movement can already inspect write, flush, and sync I/O metrics, but transfer and native copy activity are still opaque. That makes it hard to tell whether time is being spent in network transfer or local native copy work.


  ## Desired outcome

  Add DataNode volume metrics for both transfer I/O and native copy I/O with the same style of counters and percentile latency reporting used by the other file I/O metrics. The public metrics surface should include TransferIoRateNumOps, TransferIoRateAvgTime, TransferIoLatency, NativeCopyIoRateNumOps, NativeCopyIoRateAvgTime, and NativeCopyIoLatency.


  ## Acceptance signals

  When transfer or native copy work runs, the corresponding sample counts and percentile series become visible through the DataNode volume metrics instead of staying at zero or being lumped into unrelated I/O categories.

  '

2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Applications embedding the SFTP filesystem expect `close()` to be safe even when shutdown paths re-enter or superclass cleanup runs first.
6	
7	  ## Desired outcome
8	
9	  `SFTPFileSystem.close()` should guard reentrancy without skipping required superclass shutdown, so repeated close calls do not leak resources or leave the connection pool in the wrong state.

12

14	
15	  '

1	title: HADOOP-17945. JsonSerialization raises EOFException reading JSON data stored on google GCS
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Operators sometimes read JSON state from object stores such as GCS and encounter zero-byte objects, where a raw end-of-file failure does not say which path was empty.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  When `JsonSerialization.load(...)` is asked to read an empty JSON file, it should fail with a path-aware `PathIOException` that clearly says `No data in ...` instead of surfacing a bare `EOFException`.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Both load paths report the file that had no content, and callers no longer have to infer from a low-level EOF that the JSON object was empty.
16	
17	  '

1	title: HADOOP-18336.Tag FSDataInputStream.getWrappedStream() @Public/@Stable
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Library consumers sometimes need to reach through `FSDataInputStream` to the wrapped implementation in order to integrate with lower-level stream behavior, but that accessor was not clearly documented as a supported public contract.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  `FSDataInputStream.getWrappedStream()` should be treated as a stable, supported API that downstream code can rely on across releases. This is an API classification change rather than a new behavior change, so the method should keep returning the underlying `InputStream` exactly as before.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  The public API surface should mark `getWrappedStream()` as supported and stable, and callers using it should not have to change code or expectations about the returned stream instance.
16	
17	  '

1	title: HADOOP-18216. io.file.buffer.size must be greater than zero
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Operators and developers often read the default configuration file as the authoritative reference for valid setting values. The current description of `io.file.buffer.size` does not make it clear enough that non-positive values are invalid, which can lead to confusing I/O failures or hangs when someone copies an unsafe setting.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The default configuration reference should state clearly that `io.file.buffer.size` must be greater than zero. This is a documentation-only clarification, so the underlying configuration behavior does not change.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  The `io.file.buffer.size` description in the default configuration explicitly says the value must be positive, readers are less likely to choose an invalid zero or negative setting, and there is no runtime behavior change beyond the clearer documentation.
16	
17	  '

1	title: HADOOP-18321.Fix when to read an additional record from a BZip2 text file split
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Split-based text processing over BZip2 inputs depends on consistent record ownership at block boundaries, and extra reads in the wrong boundary cases can duplicate or over-consume records.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  BZip2 split readers should read one extra record only in the boundary cases that are actually required to preserve complete record delivery across splits, for both mapred and mapreduce line readers.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Record counts remain correct when splits start or end just before, at, or just after a BZip2 block boundary, instead of duplicating or over-reading records around those transitions.
16	
17	  '

1	title: HADOOP-18355. Update previous index properly while validating overlapping ranges.
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Vectored-read callers rely on early validation to reject overlapping byte ranges, but a bookkeeping bug can leave the validator comparing the wrong prior range and miss a real overlap.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  `validateNonOverlappingAndReturnSortedRanges` should update its previous-range tracking correctly while it walks the sorted list, so any overlapping pair is rejected reliably. Callers should continue to get the same failure style they already expect for overlapping requests.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Overlapping ranges must still fail with `UnsupportedOperationException` carrying the message `Overlapping ranges are not supported`, and non-overlapping ranges should continue to be returned in sorted order. The fix should be in validation accuracy, not in changing the API surface.
16	
17	  '

content.text:
You are one of ~37 parallel agents implementing change requests in an Apache Hadoop repository at /workspace (checked out at an earlier state of the real project). Your assigned batch of requirement slugs is:

yarn-router: removefromclusternodelabels-rename router-app-attempt-rest router-app-timeout-rest router-application-flow-refactor router-container-rest router-getcontainers-federation router-node-label-rest router-node-to-labels router-rmwebprotocol-methods router-pipeline-utils router-secure-login router-heapsize-env reservation-home-subcluster

The slugs are listed after the batch name (which ends with a colon). For EACH slug, in the listed order:

1. Read /workspace/requirements/<slug>.yaml in full. It describes a real Apache JIRA change (the title contains the JIRA id, e.g. HDFS-16302). Implement that change in the codebase, faithfully reproducing the upstream Apache commit where you know or can infer it. Search the codebase to find the exact files involved. Keep changes minimal and consistent with surrounding code style.

2. Commit the requirement separately using this EXACT protocol (other agents work in the same repo concurrently, so the flock and the targeted pathspecs are mandatory):

flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c '
cd /workspace
git add -A -- <only the files you changed for this requirement>
git diff --cached > requirement_patches/<slug>.diff
test -s requirement_patches/<slug>.diff
git add -f requirement_patches/<slug>.diff
git commit -m "impl: <slug>"
'

Rules:
- NEVER run plain `git add -A` or `git add .` without a pathspec, and NEVER commit changes in files you did not edit for this requirement. `git status` may show other modified/untracked files — those belong to other agents; ignore them completely, do not revert or stage them.
- The .diff file MUST be non-empty (that is what `test -s` enforces). requirement_patches/*.diff matches `*.diff` in .gitignore, so `git add -f` is required for it.
- If your batch contains a slug starting with `revert-`, first implement and commit the corresponding non-revert slug (it reverts the change of the other slug in your batch), THEN implement the revert as its own commit.
- If two slugs in your batch describe the same upstream change (duplicate JIRA), implement the change for the first one; for the second, add the remaining parts of the upstream change (extra test coverage, remaining call sites, related cleanups) so its diff is also non-empty.
- Slugs with `-docs` or doc-style titles usually touch only markdown/site files; still commit them the same way.
- Do not modify anything under /workspace/requirements/ or other agents' requirement_patches files.
- Do not attempt a full Maven build (too slow, no network guarantees). A quick targeted `mvn -o -pl <module> compile -DskipTests` is optional; prefer careful code reading. You may add tests under /workspace/agent_tests/ if useful, but it is optional.
- If a requirement turns out to be already implemented in the tree, inspect `git log --oneline | head -50` and existing requirement_patches to confirm, then find the smallest genuine remaining delta of the upstream change and commit that; only skip the slug if absolutely no delta exists, and explain in your final report.

Work through ALL slugs in your batch; do not stop early. At the end, report a compact per-slug status list (slug: committed/skipped + one-line note).

title: HADOOP-17386. Change default fs.s3a.buffer.dir to be under Yarn container path on yarn applications
category: other
requirement: 'HADOOP-17386. Change default fs.s3a.buffer.dir to be under Yarn container path on yarn applications


  ### Description of PR


  fs.s3a.buffer.dir defaults to hadoop.tmp.dir which is /tmp or similar. A lot of systems don''t clean up /tmp until reboot -and if they stay up for a long time then they accrue files written through s3a staging committer from spark containers which fail.


  Fix: use ${env.LOCAL_DIRS:-${hadoop.tmp.dir}}/s3a as the option so that if env.LOCAL_DIRS is set is used over hadoop.tmp.dir. YARN-deployed apps will use that for the buffer dir. When the app container is destroyed, so is the directory.

title: HADOOP-18330-S3AFileSystem removes Path when calling createS3Client
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  S3A client creation sometimes needs access to the filesystem URI rather than a mutable `Path` object when downstream code is deciding how to initialize request context.


  ## Desired outcome

  Internal S3A client setup should pass an explicit path URI through `S3ClientFactory.S3ClientCreationParameters.withPathUri(...)` so custom client factories can inspect the target filesystem URI without depending on a `Path` instance being threaded through. This is refactoring of the factory contract, and it must preserve existing client creation behavior for callers that do not care about the URI.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `S3ClientCreationParameters` should expose `getPathUri()` and `withPathUri(...)`, and S3A initialization should populate that field with the filesystem URI. Existing S3 client creation should continue to succeed with the same credentials, headers, and metrics wiring.

  '
=== s3a-delete-on-exit ===
title: HADOOP-18340. deleteOnExit does not work with S3AFileSystem
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Users expect `deleteOnExit` to work uniformly across Hadoop filesystems, but on S3A the registered paths were not actually being removed when the filesystem closed.


  ## Desired outcome

  S3A should honor `deleteOnExit` registrations the same way other Hadoop filesystems do, including for tracked paths that need to be deleted during shutdown. The filesystem should manage its own pending `deleteOnExit` set and use the same deletion semantics as normal deletes, without forcing callers to remember a separate cleanup path.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A path registered through `deleteOnExit` should be deleted when the S3A filesystem is closed, and the implementation should route that cleanup through the same deletion logic used for ordinary removals via `deleteWithoutCloseCheck`. If the path was never present, close should remain safe rather than turning the shutdown into a new failure.

  '
=== s3a-public-dataset-testutils ===
title: HADOOP-18168. Fix S3A ITestMarkerTool dep. on purged public bucket, introduce PublicDatasetTestUtils
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The S3A public-dataset tests currently depend on a bucket layout that has been cleaned up, which makes previously stable requester-pays and marker-tool coverage unreliable. Test maintainers need those suites to point at a still-valid public dataset and to have one place that defines which public bucket and object should be used for each scenario.


  ## Desired outcome

  The S3A test utilities should provide a shared `PublicDatasetTestUtils` helper that supplies the configured public-dataset locations for cases such as requester-pays access and large public buckets with many objects. The default requester-pays path should move to a working public dataset, while still allowing environments to override those locations or skip the tests where requester-pays or AWS-specific assumptions do not apply.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The requester-pays coverage uses a valid public object again, marker-tool tests can obtain their public dataset locations through `PublicDatasetTestUtils`, configurable overrides remain available for different environments, and incompatible environments can skip these dataset-dependent tests instead of failing against a purged bucket.

  '
=== s3a-requester-pays-support ===
title: HADOOP-14661. Add S3 requester pays bucket support to S3A
category: feature
requirement: 'HADOOP-14661. Add S3 requester pays bucket support to S3A


  ### Description of PR


  This change introduces support for "requester pays" S3 buckets (HADOOP-14661).


  There was already some discussion and patches made available (e.g. #250), although the code base has changed a bit since then.


  In summary:


  - Add some information to the main S3A documentation

  - Add example of error and how to fix/configure to troubleshooting doc

  - Add options to configure requester pays in S3A (`fs.s3a.requester-pays.enabled`) when creating S3A filesystem, which uses S3ClientFactory to create a new S3Client also taking this option

  - Add the required header inside S3ClientFactory if option was configured

  - Remove unused configuration options for requester pays in RequestFactoryImpl

  - Add new integration test which talks to publicly available `usgs-landsat` bucket (new version, not old) which is configured to require requester pays ([''usgs-landsat'' on Registry of Open Data on AWS](https://registry.opendata.aws/usgs-landsat/index.html)).

  - Add information on how to configure the new tests in testing.md


  ### How was this patch tested?


  I created an EC2 instance and an S3 Bucket in eu-west-1 and ran the tests against the global S3 endpoint.


  ```

  ```

  '
=== s3a-syncable-downgrade ===
title: 'HADOOP-17928. Syncable: S3A to warn and downgrade'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Many applications call `hflush()` or `hsync()` on S3A output streams even though S3 cannot provide real Syncable guarantees, and failing hard by default breaks otherwise workable deployments.


  ## Desired outcome

  S3A should warn and continue by default when those Syncable calls are made, while still allowing operators to restore strict rejection with `fs.s3a.downgrade.syncable.exceptions=false` when they need hard failure semantics.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The default behavior becomes tolerant for `hflush()` and `hsync()`, but deployments that opt out still receive `UnsupportedOperationException`.

  '
=== s3a-vectored-iostats ===
title: HADOOP-18227. Add input stream IOStats for vectored IO api in S3A.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using S3A vectored reads need the same visibility into performance and waste that they already have for ordinary stream reads, but vectored I/O currently leaves large observability gaps.


  ## Desired outcome

  S3A input streams should publish dedicated vectored-read IO statistics so operators can understand how often vectored reads happen, how many ranges are requested, and how many bytes are discarded as part of those reads. The counters must use the public statistic names `stream_read_vectored_operations`, `stream_read_vectored_read_bytes_discarded`, and `stream_read_vectored_incoming_ranges` so downstream tooling can consume them consistently.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Running vectored reads through S3A should update the new vectored IO counters alongside existing stream statistics. The statistics should be exposed through the standard IOStats surfaces with the exact metric names `stream_read_vectored_operations`, `stream_read_vectored_read_bytes_discarded`, and `stream_read_vectored_incoming_ranges`.

  '
=== vectored-stats-propagation ===
title: HADOOP-18392. Propagate vectored s3a input stream stats to file system stats.
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  S3A vectored reads now collect stream-level counters, but filesystem-level statistics still do not reflect that activity, leaving operators with an incomplete top-level view.


  ## Desired outcome

  Vectored-read statistics gathered by S3A input streams should be propagated up into filesystem statistics so monitoring at the filesystem layer sees the same workload patterns as stream-level diagnostics. This should enrich observability only; vectored read behavior itself must not change.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Running vectored reads through S3A should update both the input-stream counters and the aggregate filesystem statistics, including the vectored-read operation and range counters introduced for S3A. Existing vectored read success and error behavior should remain the same.

  '
=== s3autils-limitedprivate-methods ===
title: HADOOP-18016. Make certain methods LimitedPrivate in S3AUtils.java
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Some external integrations depend on selected S3AUtils helper methods, but those methods are currently undocumented as supported extension points. Integrators need a clear signal that these helpers are intentionally exposed for limited partner use.


  ## Desired outcome

  Mark the relevant S3AUtils helpers as @InterfaceAudience.LimitedPrivate("Ranger") so downstream Ranger integration can rely on them without treating the entire utility class as public API. This is an API audience clarification, not a behavior change.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The affected helper methods, including lookupPassword and the per-bucket configuration helper, are explicitly annotated for Ranger use while their existing runtime behavior stays the same.

  '
=== sts-client-shutdown ===
title: HADOOP-18397. Shutdown AWSSecurityTokenService when its resources are no longer in use
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  S3A components that request temporary credentials create AWS STS clients, but those clients may remain open longer than necessary and leak resources in long-running processes.


  ## Desired outcome

  The STS path should close `AWSSecurityTokenService` resources when they are no longer needed so repeated temporary-credential operations do not accumulate unused clients. This should be a resource-lifecycle improvement only; the credentials returned to callers and the retry behavior around STS requests must remain the same.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Code paths that create an STS client connection should close it deterministically after use, including the request-session-credentials flow. Temporary credential requests should continue to succeed and fail in the same user-visible ways, just without leaking STS resources afterward.

  '

You are one of ~37 parallel agents implementing change requests in an Apache Hadoop repository at /workspace (checked out at an earlier state of the real project). Your assigned batch of requirement slugs is:

mapreduce: appid-schema-type dbrecordwriter-write-exception distributedcache-api-decoupling

The slugs are listed after the batch name (which ends with a colon). For EACH slug, in the listed order:

1. Read /workspace/requirements/<slug>.yaml in full. It describes a real Apache JIRA change (the title contains the JIRA id, e.g. HDFS-16302). Implement that change in the codebase, faithfully reproducing the upstream Apache commit where you know or can infer it. Search the codebase to find the exact files involved. Keep changes minimal and consistent with surrounding code style.

2. Commit the requirement separately using this EXACT protocol (other agents work in the same repo concurrently, so the flock and the targeted pathspecs are mandatory):

flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c '
cd /workspace
git add -A -- <only the files you changed for this requirement>
git diff --cached > requirement_patches/<slug>.diff
test -s requirement_patches/<slug>.diff
git add -f requirement_patches/<slug>.diff
git commit -m "impl: <slug>"
'

Rules:
- NEVER run plain `git add -A` or `git add .` without a pathspec, and NEVER commit changes in files you did not edit for this requirement. `git status` may show other modified/untracked files — those belong to other agents; ignore them completely, do not revert or stage them.
- The .diff file MUST be non-empty (that is what `test -s` enforces). requirement_patches/*.diff matches `*.diff` in .gitignore, so `git add -f` is required for it.
- If your batch contains a slug starting with `revert-`, first implement and commit the corresponding non-revert slug (it reverts the change of the other slug in your batch), THEN implement the revert as its own commit.
- If two slugs in your batch describe the same upstream change (duplicate JIRA), implement the change for the first one; for the second, add the remaining parts of the upstream change (extra test coverage, remaining call sites, related cleanups) so its diff is also non-empty.
- Slugs with `-docs` or doc-style titles usually touch only markdown/site files; still commit them the same way.
- Do not modify anything under /workspace/requirements/ or other agents' requirement_patches files.
- Do not attempt a full Maven build (too slow, no network guarantees). A quick targeted `mvn -o -pl <module> compile -DskipTests` is optional; prefer careful code reading. You may add tests under /workspace/agent_tests/ if useful, but it is optional.
- If a requirement turns out to be already implemented in the tree, inspect `git log --oneline | head -50` and existing requirement_patches to confirm, then find the smallest genuine remaining delta of the upstream change and commit that; only skip the slug if absolutely no delta exists, and explain in your final report.

Work through ALL slugs in your batch; do not stop early. At the end, report a compact per-slug status list (slug: committed/skipped + one-line note).

title: HDFS-16267. Make hdfs_df tool cross platform
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using libhdfspp tooling on Windows and other non-POSIX environments still need a quick way to inspect filesystem capacity for a target path.


  ## Desired outcome

  The `hdfs_df` tool should remain available cross-platform, accept its `PATH` argument consistently, and report size, used space, and available space for the filesystem containing that path.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Help text and command execution no longer depend on POSIX-only parsing, and the same `hdfs_df` contract works across supported platforms.

  '
title: HDFS-16407. Make hdfs_du tool cross platform
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using the native `hdfs du` tool on Windows and other non-POSIX platforms need it to behave like the established Unix command instead of depending on platform-specific path handling.

  ## Desired outcome

  The cross-platform implementation should preserve the existing `hdfs du` command contract, including help output, optional path handling, and recursive traversal behavior.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The tool works consistently across platforms with the same command-line shape users already know, whether they run it with help flags, a specific path, or recursive listing.

Your PR title ...'.\n-->\n\n### Description of PR\nThe source files for `hdfs_get` uses `getopt` for parsing the command line arguments. getopt is available only on Linux and thus, isn't cross platform. We need to replace getopt with `boost::program_options` to make these tools cross platform.\n\n`hdfs_get` has the same functionality as `hdfs_copyToLocal`. Thus, we're reusing the same to implement `hdfs_get`.\n\n### How was this patch tested?\nGiven that `hdfs_get` has the same functionality as `hdfs_copyToLocal`, we've implemented `hdfs::tools::Get` by deriving from `hdfs::tools::CopyToLocal`. title: HDFS-16471. Make HDFS ls tool cross platform
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The native `hdfs_ls` tool is tied to Linux-only option parsing today, which makes a basic file-listing command unnecessarily platform-specific for developers using the native client. Teams working on Windows or other non-Linux environments still need the same listing and recursive inspection workflow.


  ## Desired outcome

  `hdfs_ls` should become cross-platform without changing the user-visible command semantics, including normal listing and recursive traversal with `-R`. The portability work must preserve the current output behavior so users can keep the same scripts and expectations while gaining non-Linux support.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `hdfs_ls` works on supported non-Linux platforms, still honors the existing path and `-R` behavior, and produces the same style of listing results users already rely on.

  '
title: HDFS-16472. Make HDFS setrep tool cross platform
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The native `hdfs_setrep` tool currently depends on Linux-only option parsing, which makes replication-management workflows unnecessarily platform-specific for teams using the native client on other operating systems. Operators and developers still need the same ability to change replication on files and recursively across directory trees regardless of platform.


  ## Desired outcome

  `hdfs_setrep` should work cross-platform while preserving its current command-line behavior for setting a target replication factor on a path and applying that change recursively when a directory is provided. This is a portability update, so the tool''s observable replication-changing behavior should remain the same while the argument parsing becomes usable beyond Linux.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `hdfs_setrep` runs on supported non-Linux platforms, still accepts the existing replication-factor and path arguments, continues to handle directory recursion as before, and changes replication in the same way users already expect from the Linux implementation.

  '
title: HDFS-16473. Make HDFS stat tool cross platform
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The native `hdfs_stat` tool currently relies on Linux-only option parsing, which keeps a basic metadata-inspection command from working consistently across development platforms. Users of the native client should be able to inspect file or directory status and get the usual error reporting on non-Linux systems too.


  ## Desired outcome

  `hdfs_stat` should become cross-platform while preserving its current command-line behavior for files, directories, and missing paths. This is a portability fix, so the tool should keep the same style of stat output and failure reporting while becoming usable beyond Linux.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `hdfs_stat` runs on supported non-Linux platforms, still reports metadata for both files and directories in the expected format, still surfaces an appropriate error for a missing path, and does not change the observable stat semantics users already rely on.

  '
title: HDFS-16474. Make HDFS tail tool cross platform
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The native `hdfs_tail` tool currently depends on Linux-only option parsing, which prevents teams using the native client on other platforms from relying on the same quick file-inspection workflow. Developers and operators still need to read the tail of an HDFS file, follow appended output, and get the usual failure reporting for missing paths regardless of operating system.


  ## Desired outcome

  `hdfs_tail` should become cross-platform while preserving its current command-line behavior, including reading the last portion of a file by default and continuing to follow appended data when `-f` is used. This is a portability fix, so the observable tail output and error semantics should remain the same while argument parsing becomes usable beyond Linux.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `hdfs_tail` runs on supported non-Linux platforms, still prints the tail of an existing file in the same way as before, continues to support follow mode with `-f`, reports an appropriate error for a missing path, and does not change the user-visible behavior of the tool apart from restoring portability.

  '

===== rbf-actual-client-ip =====
title: 'HDFS-13248: Namenode needs to use the actual client IP when going through RBF proxy.'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  In Router-based Federation deployments, the NameNode currently sees the router''s address instead of the real client address, which can break locality-sensitive decisions and send reads to less appropriate DataNodes. Operators need a safe way to forward the original client IP without letting arbitrary users spoof it.


  ## Desired outcome

  The NameNode should honor client IP information forwarded by trusted router users so data-locality decisions can use the real caller address, but only when that forwarding is allowed by `dfs.namenode.ip-proxy-users`. If the caller is not trusted, the NameNode should continue using the proxy address, and the existing audit-log behavior can remain as it is.


  ## Acceptance signals

  With `dfs.namenode.ip-proxy-users` configured for the router identity, locality decisions prefer replicas near the actual client IP; without that trust, the proxy address is still used; and the feature can be enabled or disabled administratively without changing normal RBF request routing.

  '

===== rbf-trash-short-user =====
title: 'HDFS-16628 RBF: Correct target directory when move to trash for kerberos login user.'
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  In Router-based federation, a Kerberos-authenticated HDFS user deleting data through a mount point can be sent to the wrong trash location because the full principal is treated as the home-directory name.


  ## Desired outcome

  Router trash resolution should use the short username so a mounted delete lands under the same per-user trash hierarchy that other HDFS paths use.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A user authenticated as a principal such as `randomUser/dev@HADOOP.COM` finds deleted mounted files under the short-name trash location, for example `/user/randomUser/.Trash/Current/...`, instead of under a principal-form directory.

  '

===== router-fsck-servlet-base =====
title: HDFS-16687. RouterFsckServlet replicates code from DfsServlet base class
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The Router fsck servlet had copied utility logic that already exists in the shared DFS servlet base, increasing the chance of drift between Router and NameNode behaviors.


  ## Desired outcome

  This is internal consolidation: `RouterFsckServlet` should rely on the shared DFS servlet base class instead of maintaining a duplicate implementation, while keeping the same fsck request behavior and security handling visible to users.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Router fsck requests should continue to authenticate and execute the same way they did before, but the servlet should inherit the common DFS behavior from `DfsServlet` rather than carrying a private copy.

  '

===== subcluster-router-metrics =====
title: HDFS-16313. Add metrics for each subcluster
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Router-based federation operators can see aggregate RPC health today, but that view is not enough when only one nameservice is degraded. They need per-nameservice visibility so they can tell whether traffic to ns0, ns1, and the rest is succeeding or failing independently.


  ## Desired outcome

  Expose router RPC metrics separately for each configured nameservice, not just as one global total. The per-nameservice view should track the same kinds of counters operators already use, including proxy operation activity, so a hotspot or outage in one subcluster is immediately visible.


  ## Acceptance signals

  After traffic is sent through the router, operators can inspect nameservice-specific metrics and see counters such as ProxyOp move independently for each target namespace rather than only in the global router metrics.

  '
```

=== ec-decoding-concurrent-preads ===
title: HDFS-16422. Fix thread safety of EC decoding during concurrent preads
category: bugfix
requirement: 'HDFS-16422. Fix thread safety of EC decoding during concurrent preads


  Reading data on an erasure-coded file with missing replicas(internal block of block group) will cause online reconstruction: read `dataUnits` part of data and decode them into the target missing data. Each `DFSStripedInputStream` object has a `RawErasureDecoder` object, and when we doing pread concurrently, `RawErasureDecoder.decode` will be invoked concurrently too. `RawErasureDecoder.decode` is not thread safe, as a result of that we get wrong data from pread occasionally.

  '
=== ec-decoding-invalid-buffer ===
title: HDFS-16544. EC decoding failed due to invalid buffer
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Reading an erasure-coded file that spans multiple stripes can still be recoverable even if one data block and one parity block are corrupted, but the current decode path can reuse stale state and trip over a missing buffer instead. That causes a user-visible read failure in cases where HDFS should still be able to reconstruct the requested data.


  ## Desired outcome

  EC reads should keep decoding correctly across multi-stripe files when the remaining inputs are still sufficient, including the case where one data block and the first parity block have failed. Recoverable reads should no longer fail with `Invalid buffer found, not allowing null` because a closed reader left decode bookkeeping in an invalid state for a later stripe.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Multi-stripe EC reads succeed in recoverable mixed data-and-parity corruption scenarios, decode state for later stripes is built only from the inputs that are still valid, the null-buffer failure no longer appears for these cases, and unrecoverable stripes still fail through the normal error path.

  '
=== ec-decoding-valid-inputs ===
title: HDFS-16538. EC decoding failed due to not enough valid inputs
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Clients reading erasure-coded HDFS files can still have enough surviving data to recover a stripe even when more than one block read fails, but the current decode path can stop early and raise a not-recoverable error instead. That turns a recoverable read into a user-visible failure for EC workloads that should have continued.


  ## Desired outcome

  EC reads should continue to decode successfully whenever enough valid inputs remain to reconstruct the requested data, even if more than one block read in the stripe has failed. Recoverable reads should no longer fail with `No enough valid inputs are provided, not recoverable` just because multiple source reads failed before decode bookkeeping was updated.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Reading an erasure-coded file still succeeds in recoverable multi-failure cases, decode only proceeds with the actually valid inputs that remain, the not-recoverable exception is reserved for truly unrecoverable stripes, and normal EC read behavior is unchanged outside of these previously failing cases.

  '
=== ec-decommission-performance ===
title: 'HDFS-16613. EC: Improve performance of decommissioning dn with many ec blocks'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Decommissioning a DataNode in an erasure-coded HDFS cluster can take longer than necessary when recovery work for that node is throttled like ordinary replication traffic.


  ## Desired outcome

  The NameNode should allow decommissioning datanodes to use the hard replication stream limit for erasure-coded recovery so that decommission progress is not capped by the normal stream setting.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Operators decommissioning datanodes that host many EC blocks see faster progress without having to increase the general replication stream limit for the whole cluster.

  '
=== ec-group-block-limit ===
title: HDFS-16430. Validate maximum blocks in EC group when adding an EC policy
category: feature
requirement: 'HDFS-16430. Validate maximum blocks in EC group when adding an EC policy


  HDFS EC adopts the last 4 bits of block ID to store the block index in EC block group. Therefore maximum blocks in EC block group is `2^4=16`, and which is defined here: `HdfsServerConstants#MAX_BLOCKS_IN_GROUP`.


  Currently there is no limitation or warning when adding a bad EC policy with `numDataUnits + numParityUnits > 16`. It only results in read/write error on EC file with bad EC policy. To users this is not very straightforward.

  '
=== ec-reconstruction-source-check ===
title: 'HDFS-16479. EC: NameNode should not send a reconstruction work when the source datanodes are insufficient'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  In erasure-coded HDFS, the NameNode can currently schedule reconstruction work even when there are not enough usable source DataNodes to rebuild the missing data. That creates pointless work assignments which fail downstream and surface avoidable reconstruction errors on the DataNode side.


  ## Desired outcome

  The NameNode should skip issuing EC reconstruction work when the set of non-busy source DataNodes is insufficient to recover the missing stripes. Reconstruction should still be scheduled normally once enough valid sources are available, but impossible work should be filtered out before it is sent.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Reconstruction work is not dispatched when too few usable EC sources remain, no failing work item is generated for those impossible cases, eligible blocks are still scheduled once enough sources are available, and the affected under-reconstruction blocks remain tracked without triggering avoidable DataNode-side failures.

  '
=== ec-safe-length-overflow ===
title: HDFS-16272. Fix int overflow in computing safe length during EC block recovery
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Recovery of very large erasure-coded files can overflow integer arithmetic when the safe recovery length is computed, which risks truncating at the wrong point.


  ## Desired outcome

  Safe-length calculation for EC block recovery must work correctly at large sizes and avoid 32-bit overflow so lease recovery chooses the real recoverable length.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Striped block recovery produces the correct safe length even when intermediate arithmetic would exceed the integer range.

  '
=== ec-single-dn-rack-decommission ===
title: 'HDFS-16456. EC: Decommission a rack with only on dn will fail when the rack number is equal with replication'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators using erasure coding can get stuck decommissioning a DataNode when a rack has only one node and the cluster has about as many racks as the EC placement expects. In that layout, the decommission workflow can incorrectly conclude that placement cannot be satisfied, even though the cluster should be able to rebalance across the remaining non-empty racks.


  ## Desired outcome

  Decommissioning should continue to work for EC data when a single-node rack is being drained, including cases where rack count and replica-placement limits would otherwise be calculated too strictly. Placement decisions should treat empty racks appropriately, fall back to other valid racks when an initial choice fails, and keep block placement policy satisfaction intact through the decommission process.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A DataNode can be decommissioned successfully from a one-node rack in the affected EC topology, replacement replicas are still created with valid rack distribution, non-empty rack accounting stays correct as nodes are decommissioned or recommissioned, and placement-policy checks no longer fail solely because an emptied rack is still counted against the cluster layout.

  '
=== verifyec-debug-tool ===
title: HDFS-16286. Add a debug tool to verify the correctness of erasure coding on file
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  `hdfs debug verifyEC -file <file>` should inspect each block group of a closed erasure-coded file and report whether reconstruction checks succeed.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The command emits per-block-group progress such as `Checking EC block group: blk_...`, returns `Status: OK` for healthy groups, and produces clear failures for missing files, non-files, open files, or files that are not erasure coded.

  '

title: HDFS-16375. The FBR lease ID should be exposed to the log
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Investigating full block report behavior is unnecessarily slow because the logs identify the report but not the lease that ties the report lifecycle together across DataNode and NameNode processing.

  ## Desired outcome

  Full block report logging should include the associated lease identifier everywhere operators need to correlate the send and processing flow.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The relevant log lines include the lease ID in hexadecimal form such as `0x...`, making it possible to trace a report consistently end to end.

  '
title: HDFS-16426. Fix nextBlockReportTime when trigger full block report force
category: bugfix
requirement: 'HDFS-16426. Fix nextBlockReportTime when trigger full block report force


  jira: [HDFS-16426](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HDFS-16426)


  When we trigger full block report force by command line, the next block report time will be set like this:


  nextBlockReportTime.getAndAdd(blockReportIntervalMs);


  nextBlockReportTime will larger than blockReportIntervalMs.


  If we trigger full block report twice, the nextBlockReportTime will larger than 2 * blockReportIntervalMs. This is obviously not what we want.


  We fix the nextBlockReportTime = now + blockReportIntervalMs after full block report trigger by command line.

  '

title: HDFS-16279. Print detail datanode info when process first storage report
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  When a DataNode sends its first storage report, operators often need more than a UUID to identify which machine actually reported in.


  ## Desired outcome

  The first-storage-report log message should include the detailed DataNode identity so cluster operators can immediately tell which node and storage report triggered the event.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Troubleshooting logs show richer DataNode detail instead of only the datanode UUID.

  '
title: HDFS-16391. Avoid evaluation of LOG.debug statement in NameNodeHeartbeatService
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  This is an internal logging-efficiency cleanup in Router heartbeat code, where the goal is to avoid needless string construction when debug logging is turned off.

  ## Desired outcome

  Debug-only diagnostic messages should be built lazily, while all existing heartbeat behavior and emitted logs at enabled levels remain intact.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The code no longer pays the cost of eagerly formatting namenode descriptions when debug logging is disabled, and no observable heartbeat behavior changes.

  '
title: HDFS-16623. Avoid IllegalArgumentException in LifelineSender
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A delayed DataNode can calculate a negative wait before its next lifeline, which then bubbles into scheduling code as an `IllegalArgumentException` even though the correct behavior is simply to send the lifeline immediately.


  ## Desired outcome

  Lifeline scheduling should tolerate overdue timestamps by clamping the next wait to a non-negative value instead of propagating an invalid negative delay.


  ## Acceptance signals

  When the computed lifeline deadline is already in the past, the DataNode keeps running and schedules the next lifeline without throwing an `IllegalArgumentException`.

  '

title: 'HDFS-16302. RBF: RouterRpcFairnessPolicyController record requests accepted by each nameservice'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Router-based Federation fairness metrics should show not only exhaustion and rejection but also which nameservices are successfully receiving permits.


  ## Desired outcome

  Router metrics must track accepted permits per nameservice and expose them through the JSON and MBean surface via `getAcceptedPermitsPerNsJSON`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Operators can compare accepted, rejected, and available permits per nameservice when diagnosing handler pressure.

  '
=================== rejected-permits-nameservice ===================
title: HDFS-16296. RouterRpcFairnessPolicyController add rejected permits for each nameservice
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Router-based Federation fairness can reject requests when a nameservice is overloaded, and operators need to see exactly where that pressure is happening.


  ## Desired outcome

  Router metrics should track rejected permits per nameservice and expose them through the metrics and MBean JSON surface, including `getRejectedPermitsPerNsJSON`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Dashboards can distinguish total rejections from per-nameservice rejections during overload events instead of showing only a cluster-wide number.

  '
=================== rbf-available-handler-metrics ===================
title: 'HDFS-16273. RBF: RouterRpcFairnessPolicyController add availableHandl…'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Operators running Router-based Federation need to know how many handler permits remain for each nameservice, not just the overall total across the router.


  ## Desired outcome

  Federation RPC metrics should expose per-nameservice available-handler information, including a JSON-facing metric contract through `getAvailableHandlerOnPerNs`, and return `N/A` where fairness control is not active.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Monitoring can distinguish healthy and saturated nameservices from router metrics alone, instead of only showing a cluster-wide aggregate.

  '
=================== rbf-available-ns-retry ===================
title: 'HDFS-16359. RBF: RouterRpcServer#invokeAtAvailableNs does not take effect when retrying'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  In Router-based federation, a multi-destination mount should keep working when one target namespace fails and another namespace is still available. Today invokeAtAvailableNs can lose that retry behavior because it rebuilds the candidate set incorrectly during retries.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make RouterRpcServer#invokeAtAvailableNs retry against the remaining available namespaces after one namespace has already failed, instead of effectively discarding the fallback set. This should restore the intended high-availability behavior for multi-destination mounts.


  ## Acceptance signals

  If the first namespace chosen for a multi-destination operation fails, the router retries the operation on another available namespace and can still return a successful result when an alternate namespace is healthy.

  '
=================== rbf-dynamic-handler-allocation ===================
title: 'HDFS-14750. RBF: Support dynamic handler allocation in routers'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Router-based Federation operators need fairness controls that can adapt handler capacity to real namespace traffic instead of staying fixed after startup. Static allocation can leave busy namespaces short on handlers while quieter namespaces hold unused capacity, which makes router throughput less responsive than it should be under uneven load.


  ## Desired outcome

  RBF should support a `DynamicRouterRpcFairnessPolicyController` that periodically resizes per-namespace permit capacity based on observed traffic while still enforcing configured minimum handler floors. The dynamic controller needs to honor the router handler-count settings, the minimum-per-namespace setting, and the refresh interval configuration, and it should expose the resulting capacity distribution through the existing permit-capacity JSON surface returned by `getPermitCapacityPerNs()` so operators and tests can observe the live allocation.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Routers can instantiate `DynamicRouterRpcFairnessPolicyController` as a fairness-policy option, per-namespace permit capacity is rebalanced over time according to traffic while preserving the configured minimum handler guarantees, the controller reports the current allocation through `getPermitCapacityPerNs()` as JSON, and permit acquisition behavior reflects the updated capacities rather than the static startup allocation.

  '
=================== revert-rbf-handler-allocation ===================
title: 'Revert "HDFS-14750. RBF: Support dynamic handler allocation in routers"'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS federation operators need router fairness controls to stay on the stable, predictable model rather than exposing a newer dynamic handler-allocation surface that is not ready to keep.

  ## Desired outcome

  The router should fall back to the pre-existing fairness behavior, without dynamic allocation classes, adjustable semaphores, or the extra per-namespace capacity and accept/reject metrics introduced by that experiment.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Existing permit acquisition and available-handler reporting continue to work, but the dynamic handler-allocation feature surface is absent.

  '
=================== rbf-fairness-policy-reconfigure ===================
title: 'HDFS-16539. RBF: Support refreshing/changing router fairness policy controller without rebooting router'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Operators running Router-based Federation may need to change the router fairness policy controller or refresh its handler allocation without bouncing the router process. Requiring a restart for that kind of fairness tuning creates unnecessary disruption and makes it harder to adjust live traffic handling safely.


  ## Desired outcome

  Router fairness policy control should be refreshable at runtime through the existing generic refresh mechanism, including support for changing the configured controller implementation and reloading handler allocation settings without a router reboot. The refresh contract should be exposed through the `RefreshFairnessPolicyController` handler so operators can invoke `hdfs dfsrouteradmin -refreshRouterArgs ROUTER_ADDR RefreshFairnessPolicyController` and have the router begin using the refreshed fairness policy immediately.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A router can refresh its fairness policy controller without restarting, the `RefreshFairnessPolicyController` refresh path is registered and callable through `dfsrouteradmin`, controller swaps take effect for subsequent RPC fairness decisions, prior controllers are shut down cleanly, and fairness-handler accounting reflects the refreshed configuration rather than the stale one from process startup.

  '
=================== rbf-invokeatavailablens-retry ===================
title: 'HDFS-16369. RBF: Fix the retry logic of RouterRpcServer#invokeAtAvailableNs.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  In Router-based federation, a mount that points at multiple namespaces can fail the whole client operation when one destination namespace is temporarily unavailable, even though another destination could still serve the request.

  ## Desired outcome

  When the router hits an unavailable subcluster during `invokeAtAvailableNs`, it should retry the next viable namespace so calls such as fetching server defaults can still succeed, but it should not silently retry unrelated `IOException` failures.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Operations continue through another destination when the failure is specifically an unavailable namespace, and non-retryable I/O failures are still surfaced to the caller.

  '
=================== router-fairness-handler-validation ===================
title: 'HDFS-16417. RBF: StaticRouterRpcFairnessPolicyController init fails with division by 0 if concurrent ns handler count is configured'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Router fairness control can start with too few handlers, which produces unusable per-namespace allocations and can even trigger divide-by-zero style failures during initialization.

  ## Desired outcome

  The router should reject invalid low handler counts up front instead of starting with a broken fairness-control state.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Configurations that would yield zero or otherwise invalid per-namespace permits fail clearly during initialization, and valid handler counts continue to start normally.

  '
=================== router-fairness-timeout ===================
title: 'HDFS-16671. RBF: RouterRpcFairnessPolicyController supports configurable permit acquire timeout'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  In Router-based federation, fairness throttling can protect overloaded nameservices, but a hardcoded permit wait time makes it difficult for operators to tune responsiveness for their own latency and throughput goals.


  ## Desired outcome

  Operators should be able to configure how long `RouterRpcFairnessPolicyController` waits to acquire a permit instead of being locked to a fixed one-second policy. The timeout must be controlled by `DFS_ROUTER_FAIRNESS_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT`, measured in milliseconds, and invalid negative values should fall back to `DFS_ROUTER_FAIRNESS_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Permit acquisition should use the configured `DFS_ROUTER_FAIRNESS_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` value, including allowing an immediate timeout when the value is zero. Negative settings should not break the controller; they should log a warning and continue with `DFS_ROUTER_FAIRNESS_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`.

  '
