=== slow-datanode-metrics ===
title: HDFS-16526. Add metrics for slow DataNode
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators need clearer visibility into slow DataNode behavior so they can tell whether replication or write pipelines are being delayed by local disk work or by slow acknowledgements moving upstream through the pipeline. Without dedicated counters, these cases are harder to spot and diagnose from routine monitoring.


  ## Desired outcome

  DataNode metrics should expose separate counters for these slow-path conditions so monitoring systems can distinguish them directly. The exported metric contract needs to include `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` for delayed flush or sync activity and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount` for delayed upstream acknowledgements, without changing normal write behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  DataNode metrics now publish `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount`, slow flush-or-sync events increment the former, slow upstream-ack events increment the latter, and the change adds observability only without altering the underlying pipeline semantics.

  '
=== slow-datanode-metrics-docs ===
title: HDFS-16526. Addendum Add metrics for slow DataNode
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Operators can only make use of new DataNode slow-path counters if the metrics reference material describes them clearly enough to wire dashboards and alerts against the published names. After adding the slow DataNode metrics, the user-facing metrics documentation also needs to acknowledge those counters.


  ## Desired outcome

  Hadoop''s metrics reference should document the new slow DataNode counters so operators know that `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount` are available and what conditions they represent. This is documentation-only work, so runtime behavior and metric emission stay unchanged.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The metrics documentation includes the newly added slow DataNode counters by name, operators can discover `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount` from the published reference material, and no code behavior changes beyond that documentation update.

  '
=== slow-datanode-reconfigurable ===
title: HDFS-16287. Support to make dfs.namenode.avoid.read.slow.datanode reconfigurable
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Avoiding slow DataNodes for reads is useful, but NameNode operators need to be able to turn that policy on or off without a restart.


  ## Desired outcome

  `dfs.namenode.avoid.read.slow.datanode` should become a reconfigurable NameNode setting that can be changed at runtime through the standard reconfiguration path.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Live reconfiguration updates the read-avoidance behavior immediately and rejects invalid runtime changes through the normal reconfigure flow.

  '
=== slow-node-latency-reporting ===
title: HDFS-16582. Expose aggregate latency of slow node as perceived by the reporting node
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators investigating slow peers need more than a list of suspicious DataNodes; they need to see which reporter observed the problem and how much latency was involved.

  ## Desired outcome

  The slow-peer report should carry the reporting node and observed latency for each slow node, and the tracker should return structured `SlowPeerLatencyWithReportingNode` entries instead of plain strings.

  ## Acceptance signals

  `getSlowPeersReport()` includes host identities together with latency values such as the reported 15.5, 14.5, or 18.7-style measurements, and tracker queries retain per-reporter latency data.

  '
=== slow-peer-jmx-reconfig ===
title: HDFS-16634. Dynamically adjust slow peer report size on JMX metrics
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  On busy HDFS clusters, administrators may need to increase or decrease the size of the slow peer report without restarting the NameNode, especially when cluster conditions change during an incident.


  ## Desired outcome

  `dfs.datanode.max.nodes.to.report` should be live reconfigurable so the updated limit immediately controls the slow peer report and also appears in the NameNode''s reconfigurable-properties listing.


  ## Acceptance signals

  After live reconfiguration, the slow peer report expands or contracts without a restart, and administrative tooling shows `dfs.datanode.max.nodes.to.report` among the settings that can be reconfigured at runtime.

  '
=== slow-peer-outlier-metrics ===
title: HDFS-16595. Slow peer metrics - add median, median absolute deviation and upper latency limits
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators diagnosing slow peers need more than raw latency; they need the statistical context that made a peer an outlier.

  ## Desired outcome

  Slow-peer reporting should carry an `OutlierMetrics` record with `median`, `mad`, `upperLimitLatency`, and `actualLatency`, and those values should flow through reports, JSON output, and protobuf conversions.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Slow-peer reports and downstream consumers can see the exact metric values, not just the offending node names.

  '
=== slownode-badnode-pipeline-recovery ===
title: HDFS-16348. Mark slownode as badnode to recover pipeline
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  When a write pipeline keeps receiving acknowledgements from a slow DataNode, the client can remain stuck retrying the same unhealthy path instead of rebuilding around that node. Users want the pipeline to recover automatically before the write times out.


  ## Desired outcome

  Track repeated slow-node reports in the write pipeline and treat a DataNode as bad once it has been reported slow for the configured threshold of consecutive acknowledgements. At that point the client should abandon that node and recover the pipeline rather than waiting indefinitely for the same slow peer.


  ## Acceptance signals

  After a node crosses the slow-node threshold, pipeline recovery is triggered and the failure path clearly states that a reply was received from slowNode continuously for the configured number of times, instead of leaving the client on the degraded pipeline.

  '
=== slowpeer-collect-nodes-reconfigurable ===
title: HDFS-16327. Make dfs.namenode.max.slowpeer.collect.nodes reconfigurable
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  NameNode operators may need to adjust how many slow peers are retained for reporting without scheduling a restart. Today dfs.namenode.max.slowpeer.collect.nodes behaves like a static setting, which makes live tuning awkward.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make dfs.namenode.max.slowpeer.collect.nodes live-reconfigurable on the NameNode and expose it through the standard reconfigurable-properties listing. Valid changes should take effect immediately in DatanodeManager.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Administrators can reconfigure dfs.namenode.max.slowpeer.collect.nodes at runtime, observe the updated value through the running NameNode, and see the property listed among the NameNode''s reconfigurable settings.

  '
=== namenode-slow-peer-reconfigure ===
title: HDFS-16528. Reconfigure slow peer enable for Namenode
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  NameNode operators may want to turn slow-peer tracking on or off while a cluster is running so they can manage diagnostic overhead without taking the NameNode down. Right now the `dfs.datanode.peer.stats.enabled` setting is not fully reconfigurable on the NameNode side, which makes that operational toggle less useful than related live-reconfig options.


  ## Desired outcome

  The NameNode should allow `dfs.datanode.peer.stats.enabled` to be reconfigured at runtime, with slow-peer tracking behavior updating immediately to match the new boolean value. When disabled, slow-peer reports and JSON output should stop surfacing collected data; when enabled again, the normal slow-peer tracker should resume without requiring a restart.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Administrators can reconfigure `dfs.datanode.peer.stats.enabled` on a live NameNode, the NameNode switches between enabled and disabled slow-peer tracking behavior immediately, disabled mode returns empty slow-peer results instead of stale data, and invalid non-boolean values are rejected as reconfiguration errors rather than being silently accepted.

  '

category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using DataNodePeerMetrics need dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson() to reflect only currently valid peer timing data. Stale entries should disappear once their rolling-average windows expire, otherwise the JSON keeps advertising dead peers as active.

1	title: HDFS-16259. Catch and re-throw sub-classes of AccessControlException thrown by any permission provider plugins (eg Ranger)
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Custom permission-provider plugins can throw specialized subclasses of `AccessControlException`, and flattening them loses the authorization detail operators need.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  HDFS permission checks should catch and rethrow those subclasses intact so downstream callers continue to see the original plugin-specific authorization failure type.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  A plugin-originated `AccessControlException` subclass survives the permission-check path instead of being normalized into a less specific failure.
16	
17	  '

1	title: HDFS-16274. Improve error msg for FSNamesystem#startFileInt
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  When file creation is rejected because the requested HDFS block size is too small, the current NameNode error is hard for users to interpret and tune against.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The failure should clearly state that the requested block size is below the configured minimum and point operators to `dfs.namenode.fs-limits.min-block-size` so the cause is immediately actionable.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Users can see both the requested size and the configured minimum in the error context instead of a vague size-validation failure.
16	
17	  '

1	title: HDFS-16351. add path exception information in FSNamesystem
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  When a permission or access check fails because the target path does not exist, the resulting FileNotFoundException should tell the caller which path was missing. The current generic message forces users to reproduce the issue just to identify the bad path.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Include the missing path in the FSNamesystem access-check exception so callers receive a FileNotFoundException in the form "Path not found: <path>". This improves diagnostics without changing the permission model itself.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  An access check against a nonexistent path now returns a FileNotFoundException that contains the exact path instead of the generic "Path not found" text.
16	
17	  '

1	title: HDFS-16530. setReplication debug log creates a new string even if debug is disabled
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  NameNode operations that adjust replication can pass through very hot code paths, so even debug-only logging should avoid unnecessary work when debug logging is disabled. Today the set-replication path can still build path strings just to prepare a debug message that will never be emitted.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The replication-change debug logging should incur no path-string construction cost unless debug logging is actually enabled. This is a small performance cleanup only, so the visible debug messages and replication behavior must stay the same whenever debug logging is turned on.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Disabled debug logging no longer forces path-string creation in the set-replication path, enabled debug logging still emits the same replication messages as before, and the replication operation itself is otherwise unchanged.
16	
17	  '

1	title: HDFS-16434. Add opname to read/write lock for remaining operations
2	category: feature
3	requirement: 'HDFS-16434. Add opname to read/write lock for remaining operations
4	
5	
6	  JIRA: [HDFS-16434](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HDFS-16434).

8

When analyzing some operations that hold locks for a long time, we can only find specific methods through stack. I suggest that these remaining operations be completed to facilitate later performance optimization.

11	  '

1	title: HDFS-16290.Make log more standardized when executing verifyAndSetNamespaceInfo().
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  During DataNode-to-NameNode handshake debugging, operators search logs for the transition to the ACTIVE NameNode, and inconsistent wording makes that harder.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Standardize the verify-and-set-namespace-info log text around the ACTIVE handshake without changing the handshake behavior itself.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  The relevant log line consistently says `Acknowledging ACTIVE Namenode during handshake`, making this step easier to spot in production logs.
16	
17	  '

1	title: HDFS-16305.Record the remote NameNode address when the rolling log is triggered.
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  In HA deployments, standby NameNodes may trigger remote log rolling, but the current log message does not say which peer was contacted.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  When log rolling is triggered remotely, the NameNode log should record the remote active NameNode address that was targeted.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Operators can identify the remote peer directly from the `Triggering log rolling to the remote NameNode` message.
16	
17	  '

1	title: HDFS-16408. Negative LeaseRecheckIntervalMs will let LeaseMonitor loop forever and print huge amount of log
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  A non-positive lease recheck interval can leave the NameNode lease monitor in a tight loop that floods the logs instead of failing early on bad configuration.
6	
7	  ## Desired outcome
8	
9	  `dfs.namenode.lease-recheck-interval-ms` should be validated as a strictly positive setting during initialization.
10	
11	  ## Acceptance signals
12	
13	  Invalid zero or negative values are rejected immediately, and the lease monitor no longer enters the endless noisy loop caused by a bad interval.
14	
15	  '

1	title: HDFS-16531. Avoid setReplication writing an edit record if old replication equals the new value
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Some clients repeatedly call setReplication with the same replication value a file already has, which creates unnecessary NameNode work and extra edit-log traffic even though nothing is actually changing. At scale, these no-op requests add noise and overhead without improving file state.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  A set-replication request that does not change the current replication should still be treated as a successful operation from the caller''s perspective, but it should avoid writing an edit record or doing the heavier mutation path. Audit visibility should remain intact, and files should keep the same replication they already had.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  No-op set-replication requests still succeed, the file''s replication remains unchanged, the NameNode avoids writing an unnecessary edit-log mutation for those no-op calls, and normal replication changes continue to follow the existing mutation path.
16	
17	  '

1	title: YARN-11159. Support failApplicationAttempt, updateApplicationPriority, updateApplicationTimeouts API's for Federation
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  In a federated YARN deployment, administrators expect the router to support the same application-management operations they can issue against a single ResourceManager, but some update flows still stop at the federation boundary.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The router should forward `failApplicationAttempt`, `updateApplicationPriority`, and `updateApplicationTimeouts` to the owning subcluster and expose normal success, failure, and latency accounting for those operations.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  A federated client can invoke all three APIs through the router and get the same operational result it would expect from a non-federated path, while router metrics show whether each request succeeded, failed, and how long it took.
16	
17	  '

1	title: YARN-11161. Support getAttributesToNodes, getClusterNodeAttributes, getNodesToAttributes API's for Federation
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Federated YARN users can already ask the Router for many cluster-wide views, but node attribute APIs still stop at the single-cluster boundary, which makes fleet-wide scheduling diagnostics incomplete.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The federated client path should support `getAttributesToNodes`, `getClusterNodeAttributes`, and `getNodesToAttributes` end to end so callers can retrieve cluster-wide node-attribute views from the Router instead of querying each ResourceManager separately. The Router must also publish success, failure, and latency accounting for these three operations so operators can see whether those federated lookups are healthy.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  The Router should aggregate attribute data returned from multiple subclusters into the expected API responses for `getAttributesToNodes`, `getClusterNodeAttributes`, and `getNodesToAttributes`. Router metrics must expose counters and latency tracking for those exact operation names, including `getNumSucceededGetAttributesToNodesRetrieved`, `getNumSucceededGetClusterNodeAttributesRetrieved`, `getNumSucceededGetNodesToAttributesRetrieved`, and the corresponding failed-retrieval counters.
16	
17	  '

1	title: YARN-11122. Support getClusterNodes API in FederationClientInterceptor
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Developers and operators using the federated YARN router expect the same cluster-node listing capability they already get from a non-federated ResourceManager.
6	
7	  ## Desired outcome
8	
9	  The router client path should implement the `getClusterNodes` API, merge subcluster results, and expose success, failure, and latency accounting through the router metrics surface.
10	
11	  ## Acceptance signals
12	
13	  Federated `getClusterNodes` requests return node data instead of a not-implemented error, and router metrics record both failed retrievals and successful latency for this API.
14	
15	  '

1	title: YARN-11160. Support getResourceProfiles, getResourceProfile API's for Federation
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  A federated YARN deployment should expose the same resource-profile discovery features as a single-cluster deployment, but the router still lacks support for those profile lookups.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The router should support both `getResourceProfiles` and `getResourceProfile`, merging the participating subcluster responses into normal federation-level results and recording success, failure, and latency metrics for those APIs.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Federated clients can retrieve the full profile list and an individual named resource profile through the router, and router observability includes successful and failed handling for both calls.
16	
17	  '

1	title: YARN-11169. Support moveApplicationAcrossQueues, getQueueInfo API's for Federation.
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  A federated YARN deployment should let administrators inspect queues and move applications through the router just as they would against a single ResourceManager, but those flows are still incomplete.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The router should support both `getQueueInfo` and `moveApplicationAcrossQueues`, including normal success, failure, and latency metrics for those federated operations.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Federated clients can retrieve queue details and move applications across queues through the router, and the router''s metrics surface reflects successful and failed handling of both APIs.
16	
17	  '

1	title: YARN-10122. Support signalToContainer API for Federation.
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  YARN federation already routes several application-management operations through the router, but container signaling is still missing from that federated experience.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The router should accept and forward `signalToContainer` requests, reject malformed requests clearly, and record normal success, failure, and latency metrics for that operation.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  A valid federated `signalToContainer` call reaches the owning subcluster and returns a response, invalid requests fail clearly, and router observability includes `signalToContainer` activity in its metrics.
16	
17	  '

1	title: YARN-11237. Fix Bug while disabling proxy failover with Federation
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  In federated YARN setups, disabling classic RM HA failover should not accidentally disable the separate federation failover path, but the proxy provider currently ties those decisions together too loosely.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Failover handling should continue to work when federation failover is enabled, even if RM HA auto-failover is turned off. The decision point needs to respect the federation-specific setting so Router and federation-aware clients do not lose failover protection just because non-federated HA failover is disabled.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  A configuration with `FEDERATION_ENABLED=true`, `FEDERATION_FAILOVER_ENABLED=true`, and `AUTO_FAILOVER_ENABLED=false` should still report failover as enabled for the federation-aware proxy path. Non-federated behavior should remain unchanged.
16	
17	  '

1	title: YARN-11137. Improve log message in FederationClientInterceptor
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  YARN federation operators rely on router logs to tell them which application call failed against which subcluster.
6	
7	  ## Desired outcome
8	
9	  Failure logs in `FederationClientInterceptor` should include the right request identifiers and subcluster information so operators can diagnose submission and report-retrieval issues from the logs alone.
10	
11	  ## Acceptance signals
12	
13	  The emitted warning and error messages name the affected operation and subcluster instead of printing misleading or partially formatted text.
14	
15	  '

1	title: HDFS-16610. Make fsck read timeout configurable
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  On busy HDFS clusters, `fsck` can appear idle long enough for fixed client-side network timeouts to expire even though the NameNode is still working through the request.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Operators should be able to tune the `fsck` connection and read timeouts with `dfs.client.fsck.connect.timeout` and `dfs.client.fsck.read.timeout` instead of being locked to hard-coded defaults.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  A slow but healthy `fsck` run can be kept alive by increasing those two settings, and the client no longer fails early simply because large or contended checks take longer than the built-in timeout.
16	
17	  '

3	requirement: 'HDFS-16458. [SPS]: Fix bug for unit test of reconfiguring SPS mode
4	
5	
6	  JIRA: [HDFS-16458](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HDFS-16458).
7	
8	
9	  TestNameNodeReconfigure#verifySPSEnabled was compared with itself(`isSPSRunning`) at assertEquals.

11

1	title: 'HDFS-16499. [SPS]: Should not start indefinitely while another SPS process is running'
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  HDFS operators can only run one Storage Policy Satisfier process at a time, but today a second start attempt can sit there retrying forever instead of telling the operator that SPS is already active. That makes automation and incident response confusing because a duplicate start looks hung rather than rejected.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  If SPS is started while another SPS instance is already running, the new attempt should fail immediately instead of retrying indefinitely. Operators should get a clear failure path they can act on, while normal SPS startup behavior remains unchanged when no competing process exists.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  A duplicate SPS start exits promptly, a normal single SPS start still succeeds, and operators no longer see an endless retry loop when another SPS process already owns the work.
16	
17	  '

1	title: 'HDFS-16488. [SPS]: Expose metrics to JMX for external SPS'
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  HDFS operators using the external Storage Policy Satisfier need standard JMX visibility into what that service is doing instead of relying only on logs.
6	
7	  ## Desired outcome
8	
9	  External SPS should publish a stable monitoring surface through `ExternalSPSMXBean`, backed by `ExternalSPSBeanMetrics`, so operators can inspect attempted movement state and related activity from ordinary JMX tooling.
10	
11	  ## Acceptance signals
12	
13	  The external SPS process initializes and closes its metrics cleanly, and the JMX surface exposes the attempted-item data needed for monitoring.
14	
15	  '

1	title: 'Revert "HDFS-16488. [SPS]: Expose metrics to JMX for external SPS"'
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  HDFS operators running the external Storage Policy Satisfier need the service itself to keep working, but they do not want a newly added JMX surface that is not ready to remain part of the supported management contract.
6

8	
9	  External SPS should continue operating without exposing `ExternalSPSBeanMetrics` or the `ExternalSPSMXBean` management interface, and the attempted-item internals that were temporarily made public should go back to being internal implementation detail.
10	
11	  ## Acceptance signals
12	
13	  There is no JMX bean published for external SPS, while the command-line and runtime behavior of the service stay aligned with the pre-metrics implementation.
14	
15	  '

3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  CapacityScheduler users can auto-create child queues, but the maximum allowed depth is currently fixed, which makes it impossible to relax or tighten the hierarchy limit for different parents.

15	  '

2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context

11	  ## Acceptance signals

15	  '

2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context

7	
8	  ## Desired outcome

10	  `CSMappingPlacementRule` must initialize group lookup from the ResourceManager service configuration, honoring `hadoop.security.group.mapping` and later `Groups.refresh()` updates instead of reading a conflicting scheduler-local class.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals

17	  '

7

1	title: YARN-11005. Implement the core QUEUE_LENGTH_THEN_RESOURCES OContainer allocation policy
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  YARN operators using opportunistic containers need a placement policy that first avoids long queue backlogs and then considers resource headroom, especially on clusters with more than two resource dimensions. The existing behavior does not provide that combined decision rule.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Implement the QUEUE_LENGTH_THEN_RESOURCES opportunistic allocation policy so node selection first prefers shorter opportunistic queues and then breaks ties using resource availability. Requested Resource information and multi-dimensional resource calculations should participate in the decision so the policy behaves sensibly on heterogeneous clusters.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  When the policy is enabled, nodes with shorter queues are preferred first, and among comparable queue depths the allocator chooses the node with the better resource share rather than ignoring resource pressure.
16	
17	  '

12

17	  '

2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context

7

12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals

16	
17	  '

############ ats-rollingleveldb-startup-recovery
title: YARN-9063. ATS 1.5 fails to start if RollingLevelDb files are corrupt…
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Application Timeline Service 1.5 should be able to start even when RollingLevelDB files are missing or corrupt, because operators need a recoverable service rather than a hard startup failure. Right now a broken LevelDB store can prevent ATS from coming up at all.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make RollingLevelDB-backed timeline stores recover by recreating the database when opening the existing files fails, instead of aborting service startup immediately. The recovery path should handle both missing files and corrupt files.


  ## Acceptance signals

  When the RollingLevelDB files cannot be opened, ATS startup recreates the store files and the service still starts instead of failing with a ServiceStateException on initialization.

  '
############ atsv2-hbase-classpath-order
title: YARN-11045. ATSv2 storage monitor fails to read from hbase cluster
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Clusters with ATSv2 enabled can fail to connect cleanly to HBase because the timeline-service dependencies lose precedence on the runtime classpath.

  ## Desired outcome

  The ATSv2 launch path should load its dedicated timeline-service libraries before the general YARN classpath so the HBase-compatible dependency set wins consistently.

  ## Acceptance signals

  ResourceManager and NodeManager processes with ATSv2 enabled can reach the HBase-backed timeline service without classpath-order failures.

  '
############ atsv2-hbase-guice-runtime
title: YARN-11047. ResourceManager and NodeManager unable to connect to Hbase when ATSv2 is enabled
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  When ATSv2 is enabled, ResourceManager and NodeManager can still fail to reach HBase if the runtime dependency set does not match the timeline-service requirements.

  ## Desired outcome

  The ATSv2 runtime path should use the HBase-compatible Guice stack and give the timeline-service library directory precedence over the rest of the YARN jars.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The runtime uses Guice `4.0` for this integration path, prepends the ATSv2 `lib/*` entries ahead of the regular classpath, and no longer fails to connect to HBase for dependency-order reasons.

  '
############ junit-5-ahs
title: YARN-10793. Upgrade Junit from 4 to 5 in hadoop-yarn-server-applicationhistoryservice
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The Application History Service test suite needs to stay current with the project’s supported test stack, and older JUnit 4 wiring makes that module harder to maintain alongside the rest of the codebase.


  ## Desired outcome

  This is tooling modernization: migrate the Application History Service tests to JUnit 5 while preserving the same behavioral assertions about history APIs, missing applications, and missing attempts. The module should keep testing the same contracts, only on the newer framework.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The migrated tests should still verify the same success and failure scenarios, including not-found cases, but run under JUnit 5 imports and conventions. Production code paths and public service behavior should remain unchanged.

  '
############ leveldb-confirmmutation-write
title: YARN-9874.Remove unnecessary LevelDb write call in LeveldbConfigurationStore#confirmMutation
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  `LeveldbConfigurationStore#confirmMutation` can perform an extra write even when no additional persistence work is needed, which adds unnecessary storage churn for ResourceManager configuration changes.


  ## Desired outcome

  Confirming a pending mutation should perform only the write that is actually required for the confirmed state transition while preserving the same visible configuration behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A confirmed mutation leaves the configuration store in the correct final state, and `LeveldbConfigurationStore#confirmMutation` no longer performs the redundant extra LevelDB write.

  '
############ skip-reparsed-timeline-logs
title: YARN-10975 EntityGroupFSTimelineStore#ActiveLogParser parses already …
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  ResourceManager operators using the entity-group filesystem timeline store are seeing unchanged summary and entity logs parsed over and over, which creates avoidable DFS traffic and repeated timeline-store work after each scan or restart.

  ## Desired outcome

  Once a log has been consumed, the store should remember both the last processed offset and the last processed modification time so it only resumes when new data is appended, including when recovery is enabled through `TIMELINE_SERVICE_ENTITYGROUP_FS_STORE_RECOVERY_ENABLED`.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Unchanged files are skipped on later scans, appended records are picked up exactly once, and restart recovery does not re-ingest older timeline data.

  '
############ timeline-entity-table-routing
title: YARN-9403.GET /apps/{appid}/entities/YARN_APPLICATION accesses application table instead of entity table
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators querying Timeline Service data under an application context can use generic-entity endpoints as well as system-entity endpoints, but requests for `/apps/{appid}/entities/YARN_APPLICATION` are being treated like application-table reads instead of generic entity lookups.


  ## Desired outcome

  Requests to `/apps/{appid}/entities/YARN_APPLICATION` should be handled as generic entity reads for that application context and return entity-table results, including an empty result when no matching generic entities exist.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A generic-entity request under an app context no longer pulls data from the application-specific table solely because the entity type string is `YARN_APPLICATION`.

  '
############ timeline-putentities-failfast
title: YARN-9822.TimelineCollectorWebService#putEntities blocked when ATSV2 HBase is down
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  ATS v2 writers should fail promptly and clearly when timeline storage is unavailable instead of letting `putEntities` block while the backing store is down.


  ## Desired outcome

  Before writing, the collector should use writer health information from `getHealthStatus()` to detect unavailable storage, retry only within `TIMELINE_SERVICE_CLIENT_MAX_RETRIES` and `TIMELINE_SERVICE_CLIENT_RETRY_INTERVAL_MS`, and report connection problems through `TimelineHealth.TimelineHealthStatus.CONNECTION_FAILURE` for both reader and writer health checks.


  ## Acceptance signals

  When timeline storage is down, `putEntities` stops waiting indefinitely and fails after bounded retry behavior; when storage is healthy, timeline writes continue normally.

  '
############ times-util-datetimeformatter
title: YARN-11116. Migrate Times util from SimpleDateFormat to thread-safe D…
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  YARN users and web surfaces rely on the `Times` utility for timestamp formatting and ISO-8601 parsing in code paths that may be hit concurrently.

  ## Desired outcome

  Date rendering should preserve the same human-readable and ISO-8601 representations, but use a thread-safe formatter implementation so concurrent calls do not corrupt formatted values or parse results.

  ## Acceptance signals

  `format(long)` and `parseISO8601ToLocalTimeInMillis(...)` still round-trip correctly, and elapsed-time handling keeps the existing results for valid and invalid inputs.

  '

It ensures 1606 that if the default endpoint is changed to a new region, data store in 1607 US-east is still reachable. 1608 1609 ## Configuring S3 AccessPoints usage with S3A 1610 S3a now supports [S3 Access Point](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/features/access-points/) usage which 1611 improves VPC integration with S3 and simplifies your data's permission model because different 1612 policies can be applied now on the Access Point level. For more information about why to use and 1613 how to create them make sure to read the official documentation. 1614 1615 Accessing data through an access point, is done by using its ARN, as opposed to just the bucket name. 1616 You can set the Access Point ARN property using the following per bucket configuration property: 1617 ```xml 1618 1619 fs.s3a.sample-bucket.accesspoint.arn 1620 {ACCESSPOINT_ARN_HERE} 1621 Configure S3a traffic to use this AccessPoint 1622 1623 ``` 1624 1625 This configures access to the `sample-bucket` bucket for S3A, to go through the 1626 new Access Point ARN. So, for example `s3a://sample-bucket/key` will now use your 1627 configured ARN when getting data from S3 instead of your bucket. 1628 1629 You can also use an Access Point name as a path URI such as `s3a://finance-team-access/key`, by 1630 configuring the `.accesspoint.arn` property as a per-bucket override: 1631 ```xml 1632 1633 fs.s3a.finance-team-access.accesspoint.arn 1634 {ACCESSPOINT_ARN_HERE} 1635 Configure S3a traffic to use this AccessPoint 1636 1637 ``` 1638 1639 The `fs.s3a.accesspoint.required` property can also require all access to S3 to go through Access 1640 Points. This has the advantage of increasing security inside a VPN / VPC as you only allow access 1641 to known sources of data defined through Access Points. In case there is a need to access a bucket 1642 directly (without Access Points) then you can use per bucket overrides to disable this setting on a 1643 bucket by bucket basis i.e. `fs.s3a.{YOUR-BUCKET}.accesspoint.required`. 1644 1645 ```xml 1646 1647 1648 fs.s3a.accesspoint.required 1649 true 1650 1651 1652 1653 fs.s3a.example-bucket.accesspoint.required 1654 false 1655 1656 ``` 1657 1658 Before using Access Points make sure you're not impacted by the following: 1659 - `ListObjectsV1` is not supported, this is also deprecated on AWS S3 for performance reasons; 1660 - The endpoint for S3 requests will automatically change from `s3.amazonaws.com` to use 1661 `s3-accesspoint.REGION.amazonaws.{com | com.cn}` depending on the Access Point ARN. While 1662 considering endpoints, if you have any custom signers that use the host endpoint property make 1663 sure to update them if needed; 1664 1665 ## How S3A writes data to S3 1666 1667 The original S3A client implemented file writes by 1668 buffering all data to disk as it was written to the `OutputStream`. 1669 Only when the stream's `close()` method was called would the upload start. 1670 1671 This made output slow, especially on large uploads, and could even 1672 fill up the disk space of small (virtual) disks. 1673 1674 Hadoop 2.7 added the `S3AFastOutputStream` alternative, which Hadoop 2.8 expanded.

8	  ## Desired outcome

1	title: HDFS-16339. Show the threshold when mover threads quota is exceeded
2	category: refactor
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  When a DataNode rejects a mover operation because too many mover threads are already active, operators need to know what the configured threshold actually is. The current message says the quota was exceeded but hides the quota value.

7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Keep the rejection behavior the same, but include the configured mover thread quota directly in the log message when copyBlock or replaceBlock is refused for exceeding that limit. This is an observability improvement only.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  The DataNode log now tells operators the exact quota value, for example quota=<value> is exceeded, instead of forcing them to look up the setting elsewhere.

17	  '

1	title: HDFS-16330. Fix incorrect placeholder for Exception logs in DiskBalancer
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context

8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Keep the existing DiskBalancer error messages, but log the exception as the throwable for block-pool iterator close failures, block copy failures, and unexpected runtime exceptions. This is an observability fix and should not alter recovery behavior.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  When DiskBalancer hits one of these failure paths, the logs retain the human-readable message and include the complete exception information instead of a malformed placeholder rendering.

2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Large decommission waves can stall when nodes that are lost or unhealthy keep occupying the limited tracking slots, forcing healthy nodes to wait in the queue. Cluster operators need decommissioning to keep making progress even after some candidate nodes disappear or stop heartbeating.

7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Improve the decommission monitors so unhealthy or lost DataNodes do not clog the active tracking budget and healthier nodes can be promoted from the pending queue sooner. Queue handling should favor progress and use node recency so older, unhealthy candidates can be requeued instead of blocking the entire workflow.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  If several nodes are queued for decommission and some become unhealthy, the system continues processing other eligible nodes rather than leaving the queue stuck behind the failed ones, and monitor ordering remains stable enough to verify by last-update time.
16	
17	  '

1	title: YARN-11230. [Federation] Add getContainer, signalToContainer REST APIs for Router.
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Federated YARN operators can inspect apps and attempts through the Router, but they still cannot fetch a single container record or send a signal to a container without going directly to the owning ResourceManager.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The Router should implement `getContainer` and `signalToContainer` so those actions are routed to the application’s home subcluster automatically. Input validation needs to stay explicit: missing identifiers should be rejected with the existing `Parameter error, ... is empty or null.` style messages, and invalid signal names should come back as a BAD_REQUEST response that lists the valid `SignalContainerCommand` values.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  After an application is submitted through the Router, a caller should be able to retrieve a non-null `ContainerInfo` for a specific attempt and container id via `getContainer`. `signalToContainer` should return OK for valid commands, return BAD_REQUEST for an invalid command string, and continue routing by deriving the home subcluster from the application id embedded in the container id.
16	
17	  '

1	title: YARN-11212. [Federation] Add getNodeToLabels REST APIs for Router.
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  YARN federation administrators need to inspect node-to-label assignments across the whole deployment, but the Router still lacks a federated `getNodeToLabels` REST view.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Calling `getNodeToLabels` on the Router should return a complete `NodeToLabelsInfo` map assembled from the active subclusters, rather than forcing operators to query each ResourceManager individually. The federated response should preserve the node-to-label structure clients already expect, including the `getNodeToLabels()` mapping keyed by node name.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  A successful federated lookup should return a non-empty `NodeToLabelsInfo`, and callers should be able to read the merged labels through `getNodeToLabels()`. In the routed test scenario, the response should carry entries for `node1` and `node2`, with `CPU` attached to `node1` and `GPU` attached to `node2`.
16	
17	  '

1	title: 'YARN-8900. [Router] Federation: routing getContainers REST invocations transparently to multiple RMs'
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  In a federated YARN deployment, operators can already inspect application and attempt details through the Router, but container listings still stop at the individual ResourceManager boundary.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  When someone asks the Router for containers for an application attempt through `getContainers`, the Router should fan that request out to every active subcluster and return one merged `ContainersInfo` response instead of behaving as unimplemented. Invalid or unknown application or attempt identifiers should degrade cleanly to an empty container list rather than breaking the federated view.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  A federated query for an application attempt spanning four active subclusters should come back with a single `ContainersInfo` whose `getContainers()` view contains all four containers. Requests for a nonexistent app, a malformed application id, or a malformed attempt id should return an empty `ContainersInfo`.
16	
17	  '

1	title: YARN-11220. [Federation] Add getLabelsToNodes, getClusterNodeLabels, getLabelsOnNode REST APIs for Router
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Federated YARN operators need cluster-wide visibility into label assignments, but the Router is missing several node-label REST views and cannot merge label data across subclusters.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The Router should support `getLabelsToNodes`, `getClusterNodeLabels`, and `getLabelsOnNode` as federated REST APIs so administrators can inspect label state from one place. Merged responses should preserve the existing response objects such as `LabelsToNodesInfo`, `NodeIDsInfo`, `PartitionInfo`, and `NodeLabelsInfo`, including deduplicated node lists and aggregated partition resources when the same label appears in multiple subclusters.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  A federated `getLabelsToNodes` response should merge repeated labels instead of overwriting them, and the merged `NodeIDsInfo` should carry the combined node list plus summed `PartitionInfo` resources. The Router should also return cluster labels containing `cpu` and `gpu`, and `getLabelsOnNode` should return labels `x` and `y` for `node1` while treating an unlabeled node like `node2` as an empty result rather than a failure.
16	
17	  '

1	title: YARN-6572. Refactoring Router services to use common util classes for pipeline creations.
2	category: refactor
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  YARN Router request pipelines for the client, admin, and web layers all need the same interceptor-chain assembly rules, but duplicated setup logic makes failures inconsistent and harder to debug.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  This is internal consolidation work: interceptor chains should be created through one common utility so Router services keep identical behavior while configuration and instantiation errors are reported consistently. The shared helper needs to validate that each configured class is the right interceptor type and can be linked with `setNextInterceptor`.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Pipeline creation should still honor the configured interceptor order and produce the same service behavior, but invalid classes or broken interceptor wiring should now fail through one common path with consistent `YarnRuntimeException` reporting. User-visible Router APIs and request routing outcomes should remain unchanged.
16	
17	  '

1	title: YARN-8973. [Router] Add missing methods in RMWebProtocol.
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  The Router’s RM web protocol surface is missing scheduler-configuration operations that operators already expect from a standalone ResourceManager.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The RM web protocol should include the missing scheduler configuration endpoints so Router deployments can forward both reads and updates without forcing operators to bypass federation for those tasks. In particular, the protocol needs to support `updateSchedulerConfiguration` and `getSchedulerConfiguration` with the same request and response style users already expect.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  A Router-backed RM web protocol implementation should expose `updateSchedulerConfiguration(...)` and `getSchedulerConfiguration(...)`, forwarding them through to the target web service. Existing Router endpoints should continue working unchanged.
16	
17	  '

1	title: '[YARN-10998] Add YARN_ROUTER_HEAPSIZE to yarn-env for routers'
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  YARN Router processes often need a different heap size from other daemons, and today administrators do not have a dedicated environment knob for that process.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Router JVM sizing should be configurable independently through `YARN_ROUTER_HEAPSIZE` in both Unix and Windows startup flows.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Router launch scripts honor `YARN_ROUTER_HEAPSIZE` without forcing operators to change the global YARN heap defaults.
16	
17	  '

1	title: YARN-6539. Create SecureLogin inside Router.
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  A secure YARN Router needs its own Kerberos login path rather than relying on borrowed assumptions from other daemons, otherwise federated services cannot be hardened cleanly.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The Router should support an explicit secure-login configuration of its own, including dedicated keytab and principal settings, so operators can run the Router as a properly authenticated Kerberos service. The relevant configuration surface needs to include `ROUTER_KEYTAB` and `ROUTER_PRINCIPAL` and use them during Router startup.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  A secured Router deployment should be able to authenticate using the Router-specific keytab and principal settings without depending on another daemon’s login path. Existing unsecured Router setups should continue to start without requiring Kerberos configuration.
16	
17	  '

1	title: YARN-11235. Refactor Policy Code and Define getReservationHomeSubcluster
2	category: refactor
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Reservation placement in YARN federation follows the same policy family as application placement, but the router policy code had grown repetitive and made reservation routing harder to support consistently.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  This is internal policy refactoring: the shared router-policy layer should be cleaned up so reservation routing can use a first-class `getReservationHomeSubcluster` path while existing policy decisions for applications remain consistent. The goal is maintainable policy code and a clearer contract for reservation placement, not a change in externally visible routing semantics.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Router policy implementations should continue honoring blacklist and active-subcluster constraints while exposing reservation home-subcluster selection through the common policy facade. Existing application routing behavior and public policy names should stay compatible.
16	
17	  '

hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs/src/site/markdown/TransparentEncryption.md:23:HDFS implements *transparent*, *end-to-end* encryption. Once configured, data read from and written to special HDFS directories is *transparently* encrypted and decrypted without requiring changes to user application code. This encryption is also *end-to-end*, which means the data can only be encrypted and decrypted by the client. HDFS never stores or has access to unencrypted data or unencrypted data encryption keys. This satisfies two typical requirements for encryption: *at-rest encryption* (meaning data on persistent media, such as a disk) as well as *in-transit encryption* (e.g. when data is travelling over the network).

hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs/src/site/markdown/HdfsDesign.md:152:The HDFS namespace is stored by the NameNode. The NameNode uses a transaction log called the EditLog to persistently record every change that occurs to file system metadata. For example, creating a new file in HDFS causes the NameNode to insert a record into the EditLog indicating this. Similarly, changing the replication factor of a file causes a new record to be inserted into the EditLog. The NameNode uses a file in its local host OS file system to store the EditLog. The entire file system namespace, including the mapping of blocks to files and file system properties, is stored in a file called the FsImage. The FsImage is stored as a file in the NameNode’s local file system too.
hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs/src/site/markdown/HdfsDesign.md:154:The NameNode keeps an image of the entire file system namespace and file Blockmap in memory. When the NameNode starts up, or a checkpoint is triggered by a configurable threshold, it reads the FsImage and EditLog from disk, applies all the transactions from the EditLog to the in-memory representation of the FsImage, and flushes out this new version into a new FsImage on disk. It can then truncate the old EditLog because its transactions have been applied to the persistent FsImage. This process is called a checkpoint. The purpose of a checkpoint is to make sure that HDFS has a consistent view of the file system metadata by taking a snapshot of the file system metadata and saving it to FsImage. Even though it is efficient to read a FsImage, it is not efficient to make incremental edits directly to a FsImage. Instead of modifying FsImage for each edit, we persist the edits in the Editlog. During the checkpoint the changes from Editlog are applied to the FsImage. A checkpoint can be triggered at a given time interval (`dfs.namenode.checkpoint.period`) expressed in seconds, or after a given number of filesystem transactions have accumulated (`dfs.namenode.checkpoint.txns`). If both of these properties are set, the first threshold to be reached triggers a checkpoint.
hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs/src/site/markdown/MemoryStorage.md:80:This step is crucial. Without the RAM_DISK tag, HDFS will treat the `tmpfs` volume as non-volatile storage and data will not be saved to persistent storage. You will lose data on node restart.
hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs/src/site/markdown/HdfsPermissionsGuide.md:171:The super-user is the user with the same identity as the NameNode process itself. Loosely, if you started the NameNode, then you are the super-user. The super-user can do anything in that permissions checks never fail for the super-user. There is no persistent notion of who was the super-user; when the NameNode is started the process identity determines who is the super-user for now. The HDFS super-user does not have to be the super-user of the NameNode host, nor is it necessary that all clusters have the same super-user. Also, an experimenter running HDFS on a personal workstation, conveniently becomes that installation's super-user without any configuration.

payload.output:
225	    It is desirable for correctness of the system that only one NameNode be in
226	    the Active state at any given time. **Importantly, when using the Quorum
227	    Journal Manager, only one NameNode will ever be allowed to write to the
228	    JournalNodes, so there is no potential for corrupting the file system metadata
229	    from a split-brain scenario.** However, when a failover occurs, it is still
230	    possible that the previous Active NameNode could serve read requests to
231	    clients, which may be out of date until that NameNode shuts down when trying to
232	    write to the JournalNodes. For this reason, it is still desirable to configure
233	    some fencing methods even when using the Quorum Journal Manager. However, to
234	    improve the availability of the system in the event the fencing mechanisms
235	    fail, it is advisable to configure a fencing method which is guaranteed to
236	    return success as the last fencing method in the list. Note that if you choose
237	    to use no actual fencing methods, you still must configure something for this
238	    setting, for example "`shell(/bin/true)`".
239	
240	    The fencing methods used during a failover are configured as a
241	    carriage-return-separated list, which will be attempted in order until
242	    one indicates that fencing has succeeded. There are two methods which ship with
243	    Hadoop: *shell* and *sshfence*. For information on implementing your own custom
244	    fencing method, see the *org.apache.hadoop.ha.NodeFencer* class.
245	
246	    - - -
247	
248	    **sshfence** - SSH to the Active NameNode and kill the process
249	
250	    The *sshfence* option SSHes to the target node and uses *fuser* to kill the
251	    process listening on the service's TCP port. In order for this fencing option
252	    to work, it must be able to SSH to the target node without providing a
253	    passphrase. Thus, one must also configure the
254	    **dfs.ha.fencing.ssh.private-key-files** option, which is a
255	    comma-separated list of SSH private key files. For example:
256	
257	            <property>
258	              <name>dfs.ha.fencing.methods</name>
259	              <value>sshfence</value>
260	            </property>
261	
262	            <property>
263	              <name>dfs.ha.fencing.ssh.private-key-files</name>
264	              <value>/home/exampleuser/.ssh/id_rsa</value>
265	            </property>
266	
267	    Optionally, one may configure a non-standard username or port to perform the
268	    SSH. One may also configure a timeout, in milliseconds, for the SSH, after
269	    which this fencing method will be considered to have failed. It may be
270	    configured like so:

15	Hadoop Auth, Java HTTP SPNEGO - Server Side Configuration
16	=========================================================
17	
18	Server Side Configuration Setup
19	-------------------------------
20	
21	The AuthenticationFilter filter is Hadoop Auth's server side component.
22	
23	This filter must be configured in front of all the web application resources that required authenticated requests. For example:
24	
25	The Hadoop Auth and dependent JAR files must be in the web application classpath (commonly the `WEB-INF/lib` directory).
26	
27	Hadoop Auth uses SLF4J-API for logging. Auth Maven POM dependencies define the SLF4J API dependency but it does not define the dependency on a concrete logging implementation, this must be addded explicitly to the web application. For example, if the web applicationan uses Log4j, the SLF4J-LOG4J12 and LOG4J jar files must be part part of the web application classpath as well as the Log4j configuration file.
28	
29	### Common Configuration parameters
30	
31	*   `config.prefix`: If specified, all other configuration parameter names
32	    must start with the prefix. The default value is no prefix.
33	
34	*   `[PREFIX.]type`: the authentication type keyword (`simple` or \
35	    `kerberos`) or a Authentication handler implementation.
36	
37	*   `[PREFIX.]signature.secret.file`: When `signer.secret.provider` is set to
38	    `file`, this is the location of file including the secret used to sign the HTTP cookie.
39	
40	*   `[PREFIX.]token.validity`: The validity -in seconds- of the generated
41	    authentication token. The default value is `36000` seconds. This is also
42	    used for the rollover interval when `signer.secret.provider` is set to
43	    `random` or `zookeeper`.
44	
45	*   `[PREFIX.]cookie.domain`: domain to use for the HTTP cookie that stores
46	    the authentication token.
47	
48	*   `[PREFIX.]cookie.path`: path to use for the HTTP cookie that stores the
49	    authentication token.
50	
51	*   `signer.secret.provider`: indicates the name of the SignerSecretProvider
52	    class to use. Possible values are: `file`, `random`,
53	    `zookeeper`, or a classname. If not specified, the `file`
54	    implementation will be used; and failing that, the `random`
55	    implementation will be used. If "file" is to be used, one need to specify
56	    `signature.secret.file` and point to the secret file.
57	
58	### Kerberos Configuration
59	
60	**IMPORTANT**: A KDC must be configured and running.
61	
62	To use Kerberos SPNEGO as the authentication mechanism, the authentication filter must be configured with the following init parameters:
63	
64	*   `[PREFIX.]type`: the keyword `kerberos`.
65	
66	*   `[PREFIX.]kerberos.principal`: The web-application Kerberos principal
67	    name. The Kerberos principal name must start with `HTTP/...`. For
68	    example: `HTTP/localhost@LOCALHOST`. There is no default value.
69	
70	*   `[PREFIX.]kerberos.keytab`: The path to the keytab file containing
71	    the credentials for the kerberos principal. For example:
72	    `/Users/tucu/tucu.keytab`. There is no default value.
73	
74	**Example**:

78	        ...

cd /workspace && export LC_ALL=C && git diff | python3 - <<'EOF'
import sys, re, subprocess
diff = sys.stdin.read()
files = {}
cur = None
removed = []
for line in diff.splitlines():
    m = re.match(r'\+\+\+ b/(.*)', line)
    if m:
        if cur and removed: files[cur] = removed
        cur = m.group(1); removed = []
    elif line.startswith('-import ') and cur:
        removed.append(line[1:])
if cur and removed: files[cur] = removed
bad = 0
for f, imps in files.items():
    content = open(f).read()
    # strip import lines
    body = '\n'.join(l for l in content.splitlines() if not l.startswith('import '))
    for imp in imps:
        name = imp.rstrip(';').split()[-1].split('.')[-1]
        if re.search(r'\b'+re.escape(name)+r'\b', body):
            print("STILL USED:", f, imp); bad += 1
print("checked", len(files), "files;", bad, "problems")
EOF
